establishes: The orders constituting these inquiries were not read. Outcomes of the magisterial and state judicial inquiries were not found.

title: The BHU Vice-Chancellor ordered a judicial inquiry led by a retired Allahabad High Court judge, reported on 26 September 2017 after an executive council meeting
establishes: Judge's name differs across sources; the order was not read. This is a university inquiry, separate from the state's.

title: The BHU inquiry committee headed by a former High Court judge released its findings on 25 April 2018, per The Wire's LiveWire. It is reported to have given the
establishes: Single source and an opinion-leaning piece. The report text was not found. Not read for what it says about who ordered the police action. Treat as unverified until the report is obtained.

title: BHU Chief Proctor O N Singh resigned on 26 September 2017, reported as taking 'moral responsibility' for the molestation of a student and the police violence th
establishes: Resignation is reported as a fact; the reason is the press's description. No document names the Proctor as having requested or ordered police action.

title: Vice-Chancellor Tripathi went on leave on 2 October 2017 citing personal reasons, and the BHU registrar was appointed interim Vice-Chancellor on 4 October 2017,
establishes: Single dated source.

title: The National Human Rights Commission sought a detailed report on the incident from the Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police and the Vic
establishes: NHRC case number and notice were not found. Replies, if filed, would be primary evidence on the chain of command.

title: Aaj Tak reports (25 September 2017) that the Prime Minister and the BJP president spoke to the Chief Minister and asked him to take necessary steps. Outlook say
establishes: Sourcing of the conversation is not given in either article.

title: No Allahabad High Court order, petition or commission report on the BHU events of 21 to 24 September 2017 was found in this research.
establishes: Searches of news coverage returned no High Court proceeding. Indian Kanoon and the eCourts portal were not searched in this pass and should be before concluding no case exists. The only judge-led inquiry found is the university's (HIST-BHU-014).

title: Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel entered the Jamia Millia Islamia campus in the evening of 15 December 2019 and used force and tear gas there. The Delhi
establishes: The occurrence is established by a court judgment that recites the NHRC's findings and by the police's own account to a magistrate (secondary report of the action taken report). The court makes no finding that any individual officer acted unlawfully and says its conclusion is not an approval of every act attributed to police (para 92). Time of entry is DISPUTED between sources: the petitioners' case in the judgment (para 12) says about 4:00 p.m.; Wikipedia (tertiary and independently unchecked) says 6:46 p.m. The judgment does not fix a time.

title: On 13 December 2019 a march by Jamia students towards Parliament was stopped near the campus. The petitioners' case, as recited in the Delhi High Court judgment
establishes: The judgment (para 11) records this as the petitioners' case only. Wikipedia (tertiary) says 50 students were detained on 13 December; that count was not checked against its cited news sources and is not repeated as established. No document read here says who gave any order on 13 December. The 13 December events are far less documented than 15 December.

title: Who gave the order to enter the campus on 15 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document read for this record names the person or the office that ordered the en
establishes: Level of office: the only institution all sources attribute the entry to is the Delhi Police (with Rapid Action Force personnel, para 18 of the judgment). The rank at which the decision was taken (station, district, range, headquarters, or the Union Home Ministry, to which Delhi Police reports) is unknown. The judgment records no police counter-affidavit statement naming a commander. The NHRC report (read only through summaries) is also reported as naming no one. The Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southeast) is named in a Scroll.in report only as an official who declined to comment on the firing inquiry; no document says he gave any order and this archive makes no such claim. Documents that could settle it are listed at HIST-JMI-020 to HIST-JMI-023.

title: Who gave the order to use tear gas, including inside the library: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Delhi Police action taken report, as reported, says officials 'used tear
establishes: The NHRC recommendation of action against personnel who used tear gas in the library is reported by two outlets, but the report itself was not read and no action against any identified officer has been found (see HIST-JMI-018). Whether the tear gas was fired on an order from a supervisor or on individual decision is not stated in any document read.

title: Who gave the order to use lathis or other force against students, and who ordered detentions: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Delhi Police action taken report, as reported
establishes: The two police accounts are in tension on the word 'detained'. See HIST-JMI-009 for the counts. A reply to the affidavit and the case diary entries would show who was in command at Kalkaji and New Friends Colony stations (the stations to which detained students were taken, per para 13 of the judgment).

title: Who gave the order to fire gunshots on 15 December 2019, if any were fired: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Indian Express, as relayed by Scroll.in on 5 January 2020, repo
establishes: Single outlet relaying another outlet; the inquiry document was not seen. Two FIRs on the violence were reported not to mention firing. The Wikipedia entry cites news reports of gunshot injuries to named persons; police said some wounds could be from tear gas shells (Wikipedia, tertiary, not independently checked). The case diary holding the statements was reportedly not yet with the Crime Branch SIT at that date.

title: Jamia's Vice-Chancellor, Najma Akhtar, said on 16 December 2019: 'Police entered the campus without permission.' The Chief Proctor, Waseem Ahmed Khan, is report
establishes: This corroborates that the university said permission was not given. It does not settle whether permission was required: the judgment (paras 85, 86 and 89) holds that informing university authorities is ordinarily expected but 'cannot ... operate as an absolute condition' where there is an immediate threat, and the Model Police Manual is cited as contemplating informing the head of an institution 'as far as possible'. No document read shows police asking for or being refused permission, or a police statement either way. The NHRC, as summarised by The Leaflet, also recorded that the university administration showed 'abject failure' in communication with police.

title: The Delhi Police position is that entry was necessary. Action taken report of 16 March 2020, as reported: police were 'forced to enter' Jamia 'to rescue the inn
establishes: These are allegations of fact by the police and the Ministry, attributed to them, and are contested by the petitioners and the university (HIST-JMI-007). The three accounts come from different filings and a Parliament reply, so they are independent of each other. Contemporary police statements are reported to have denied entering the library (Scroll.in, 20 February 2020) before library CCTV footage released on 15 February 2020 showed otherwise per the Jamia Coordination Committee (Wikipedia, tertiary).

title: Detention counts for 15 December 2019 conflict. Delhi Police action taken report (16 March 2020), as reported by The Quint: 52 persons temporarily apprehended u
establishes: No source read gives a verified count. The 52 and the 15 are official figures reported second-hand. The counts may measure different things (apprehended, detained, formally arrested), and no document read defines them. A station-wise detention register, the case diary and the Delhi Police Act section 65 records would resolve this.

title: Injury counts conflict. Home Ministry written reply in the Lok Sabha, as reported by The Leaflet on 4 February 2020: 62 police personnel and 127 persons, includ
establishes: The official figure and the media estimates are not reconciled in any document read. One person, a law student, is reported by Scroll.in to have lost an eye in the library; that is his account to The Hindu, relayed by Scroll.in, and the court did not adjudicate it. Hospital admission registers at Al-Shifa, Holy Family, AIIMS and Safdarjung hospitals (named in Wikipedia, tertiary) were not read.

title: FIRs on the 15 December 2019 violence: FIR No. 242/2019 at Police Station New Friends Colony and FIR No. 298/2019 at Police Station Jamia Nagar, both under IPC
establishes: Read in the judgment of 5 October 2026; the FIRs themselves were not read. The judgment says arrests were made and 'certain facets' remain under further investigation. The Home Ministry told the Lok Sabha on 4 February 2020 that three cases were registered (The Leaflet, secondary), and Scroll.in reported on 5 January 2020 that the Crime Branch SIT was leading inquiry into 10 rioting cases from 16 December 2019. The numbers differ, and the relationship between them is not established. These FIRs are against protesters and unnamed rioters. No FIR against any police officer was registered (HIST-JMI-012).

title: No FIR has been registered against any police officer for the 15 December 2019 campus action, on the documents read. Jamia Millia Islamia applied under section
establishes: Dismissal and its ground are verified from the judgment. The magistrate's order was not read; the quoted reasoning is Maktoob's account. Conflict: Maktoob reported on 4 February 2021 that the university's lawyers said they would file a revision petition; the 2026 judgment says no challenge was made. The judgment is later and is the primary source, so it is preferred, but no revision record was searched. In January 2020 Vice-Chancellor Akhtar said police had refused to register an FIR on the university's complaint (The Leaflet, relaying her statement).

title: The NHRC acted on complaints about Jamia. Press release of 20 December 2019: the Commission received complaints alleging illegal detention of students and denia
establishes: The press release gives no case number. The NHRC's report itself was not located or read; its content is taken from the judgment's summary (para 18 and paras 42, 68) and from news summaries (HIST-JMI-014). News summaries say the team took testimony from 94 students; that figure was not found in a document read. The NHRC case number should be requested.

title: The NHRC report dated 18 May 2020, as summarised by LiveLaw, The Wire and The Leaflet, found the protest had turned unlawful and violent; said police 'seeing no
establishes: Update 10 October 2026: the NHRC's own account of these findings, from its newsletter and Annual Report, is now in the archive (HIST-HRC-002 to HIST-HRC-004) and is the better source. The words attributed to the report here come from press summaries and differ in places from the NHRC's own wording, for example 'not a state policy rather it was an individual act' for the tear gas. The report itself was not read. Three outlets summarise it consistently and the judgment confirms the core (violence by protesters, lack of restraint in the library, tear gas avoidable, university lapses, compensation and accountability recommendations). Critics, including petitioners, said it favoured the police; that is their allegation. The report is described as neutral by the High Court (para 68). It names no officer who ordered entry or force, as far as the summaries show.

title: Delhi Police inquiries into its own conduct: (1) an administrative inquiry into alleged police atrocities in the library by the Additional Commissioner of Polic
establishes: The Leaflet writes that no punitive action appears to have been taken after the administrative inquiry; that is the outlet's reading only. The Delhi High Court judgment mentions none of these inquiries by name. Scroll.in reported Special CP (Crime Branch) Praveer Ranjan saying 'Sequence of events to be established' and that the crowd in the library 'includes students as well as outsiders'.

title: Delhi High Court judgment of 5 October 2026 (Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain; reserved 24 July 2026) dismissed the batch of eight writ petitions (lead:
establishes: Read in full from a PDF copy hosted by Verdictum; the court's own site was not checked and the file's sha256 is recorded. The court held police entry on 15 December 2019 followed escalation outside and the crowd moving in (paras 81 and 82), that prior permission is not an absolute condition (para 86), that the NHRC report presents 'a neutral picture rather than one-sided' (para 68), and that the disputed facts cannot be resolved in writ jurisdiction (para 67). Related issues are said by one outlet (not read) to remain before the Supreme Court. Appeal status not searched.

title: Earlier court steps. Supreme Court order of 17 December 2019 in W.P.(Crl) 370/2019 (Alumni Association, Jamia Millia Islamia University v. Union of India) decli
establishes: Date conflict: The Leaflet says the Chief Justice of India refused on 16 December 2019 in court; the judgment dates the order 17 December 2019. The judgment is primary and preferred for the order date. Bar & Bench reports the High Court directed affidavits; its report does not record any ruling on police entry. In August 2020 a Delhi High Court division bench is reported by The Leaflet to have observed that the NHRC report says 'the entire police action was not handled very professionally'; single source, wording not verified.

title: No disciplinary, criminal or departmental action against any police or RAF personnel for the Jamia campus events has been found in any document read. The Delhi
establishes: Absence in the documents read is not evidence that none exists. The Leaflet writes that no punitive action appears taken. Whether the Delhi government paid any compensation on the NHRC recommendation is not established; the judgment says no material shows the petitioners pursued the recommendation.

title: Civil society and press documentation on Jamia, 13 and 15 December 2019: (a) People's Union for Democratic Rights fact-finding report 'Bloody Sunday', released
establishes: Allegations by PUDR are attributed to PUDR; the report itself was not read, only The Wire's summary. The CCTV footage was not viewed. The Wire article on 25 CCTV cameras damaged (Jamia to the HRD ministry) was found by title only and its text was not read, so it is not cited for any fact.

title: Records that could be requested to answer who gave the order: the Delhi Police action taken report filed on 16 March 2020 before Metropolitan Magistrate Rajat G
establishes: Court records are not subject to refusal on the ground of an ongoing investigation the way an RTI reply may be. These filings exist; the full texts were not read. The judgment cites the 5 May 2023 affidavit (para 20) and the police counter-affidavit (para 31).

title: Records that could be requested from Delhi Police and the Home Ministry: duty rosters for 15 December 2019 at the Jamia Nagar, New Friends Colony and Kalkaji po
establishes: Existence of the rosters, the firing inquiry and the administrative inquiry is reported by the cited outlets and remains unseen. Delhi Police reports to the Union Home Ministry, so an RTI to Delhi Police and a parallel one to the Ministry of Home Affairs is the pattern described in SOURCING.md. No RTI has been filed from this research. Exemptions for investigations may be claimed.

title: Records that could be requested from the NHRC: the case file for the Jamia complaints, the investigation team's report, the report of the Commission dated 18 Ma
establishes: The Commission is reported to have recommended that the Police Commissioner and the CRPF Director General identify Delhi Police and RAF personnel seen in CCTV footage; whether they replied is not established. The case number is not on the press release read.

title: Records that could be requested from Jamia Millia Islamia: the university's complaint and executive council resolution (January 2020), the Registrar's letter of
establishes: The Registrar's letter dated 20 December 2019 is referred to in LiveLaw's account of the NHRC report. The Tribune records the Vice-Chancellor saying on 16 December 2019 she would present facts to the HRD minister. A central university is a public authority under the RTI Act in the ordinary way, but this was not checked against a source in this research.

title: Level of office at which the decision to enter, to use force and to use tear gas was taken, summary: ESTABLISHED that the actors were Delhi Police and Rapid Act
establishes: Summary record. The standing view of the archive is that where an order was given orally, the most it can establish is who was present and what was logged. Nothing read shows an order of any kind.

title: Police and paramilitary personnel (Rapid Action Force) entered the Aligarh Muslim University campus on the evening and night of 15 December 2019 during an anti-
establishes: Occurrence is not in dispute between the petitioner, the State and the University. What force was used is contested: the State's counter affidavit, as reported, says water cannons and tear gas were used and no lethal weapon; students allege rubber bullets, pellets and stun grenades. See HIST-AMU-006. No finding on proportionality.

title: The Registrar of Aligarh Muslim University issued a notice on 15 or 16 December 2019 closing the university until 5 January 2020 and asking students to vacate h
establishes: The Caravan interview (31 December 2019) says the university was closed until 5 January. A search summary alone attributed a closure notice to Registrar Abdul Hamid citing 'disturbances created by certain anti-social elements'; that attribution is unverified. SCC Online Times reports the petitioner's account that notices to vacate hostels were issued on 16 December 2019. The notice itself was not seen. Date of the notice varies by source.

title: Internet services in Aligarh were suspended from 10 pm on 15 December 2019 to 10 pm on 16 December 2019, on the order of the District Magistrate of Aligarh, Cha
establishes: OFFICE-LEVEL ANSWER: District Magistrate, Aligarh. ETV Bharat (16 December 2019) names DM Chandra Bhushan Singh; WION (22 December 2019) says the District Magistrate ordered it and quotes him that services stay suspended 'from 10 pm tonight till 10 pm tomorrow'. The order itself was not seen, so its legal basis (statute and rules invoked) and any confirmation by the state Home Department are not established. Name given by one outlet only; both outlets attribute to the DM. Both are news reports of a statement, which makes them secondary sources. The shutdown tracker internetshutdowns.in lists the same hours and classes it as mobile, citing News18, but its entry is dated 14 December 2019 on its face, which is before the event; treated as unreliable for date and not used for confidence.

title: The State of Uttar Pradesh's counter affidavit in the Allahabad High Court, filed for the Inspector General (Law and Order) and the SSP Aligarh, as reported, st
establishes: OFFICE-LEVEL ANSWER (State's account): the State says the district administration entered the campus after a request from the University Registrar. It attributes the decision to 'the administration' only. The affidavit was not read; this is SCC Online Times' summary of the January 2020 order (Mohd. Aman Khan v. Union of India, Criminal Misc. PIL/Petition No. 26085 of 2019). Sabrang's report confirms the affidavit was filed for the IG (Law and Order) and the SSP and that it alleges breach of Section 144, but did not state the Registrar-letter detail in the text fetched. An allegation by the State, attributed to it.

title: The Vice Chancellor of AMU, Tariq Mansoor, said publicly that the administration was 'left with no other choice but to call the police' and that the decision wa
establishes: OFFICE-LEVEL ANSWER (University's account): the University administration says it called the police. The Quint (25 December 2019, updated 6 January 2020) quotes the Vice Chancellor; The Leaflet reports the University's position as 'being called by the University authorities'. The written request or letter was not seen. Contested by the AMU Students' Union president, who told The Caravan (31 December 2019) that the Vice Chancellor and Registrar had accepted giving written permission for police to enter and use 'appropriate force'; this is a claim by the student leader and is not independently confirmed in that article. The Karwan e Mohabbat fact-finding report (17 December 2019 visit) records that the Vice Chancellor claims to have invited the forces, says the Registrar, Proctor and Vice Chancellor cited stone throwing, and states the team suspected the invitation papers may have been signed after entry, which it said needs verification. That is the report's suspicion and remains unproven. Scroll.in reports that AMU said police entered a hostel without permission, which is a separate point from the call for police. Who inside the University signed is not established. Timing of the request relative to entry is not established.

title: Counts disputed. Detained: 26 persons detained, 15 of them not University students according to the University and the State's affidavit as reported; the AMU De
establishes: Versions: (a) State and University, via the court record: 26 detained, 15 non-students (Leaflet). (b) AMU Deputy Proctor Azam Malik Khan, 18 December 2019: 'Out of the 26 people arrested, only 6 were AMU students' (Sabrang). (c) SSP: 21 arrested, FIR against 56 and others unidentified (Quint). (d) Teachers and doctors in the fact-finding report: around 100 picked up, around 100 injured, 20 seriously (an estimate by the team, unsupported by a count). (e) Quint: around 70 students wounded, DIG Aligarh and SP City among injured. (f) NHRC recommendation as reported by SCC Online Times: compensation for six grievously injured students. No official hospital or police tally was seen. Do not choose between them.

title: FIRs: the SSP told PTI an FIR was lodged against 56 persons and others unidentified. The Karwan e Mohabbat report says FIRs named 12 to 13 students and about 70
establishes: These may describe different FIRs on different dates (the 1,200 figure is tied by two outlets to the 23 December march, the 56 figure to 15 December, the 700 figure by The Caravan to a 10 December march). Whether they are the same FIR is not established. FIR copies were not seen. Allegations of offences are the police's and remain unproven.

title: Section 144 CrPC prohibitory orders were in force in Aligarh on 15 December 2019, according to the State's counter affidavit as reported. Who issued the order,
establishes: OFFICE-LEVEL ANSWER: NOT ESTABLISHED. Under the CrPC such an order is issued by the District Magistrate or another authorised Executive Magistrate, but no document or report read names the issuing office or gives its date and text. The Quint says the article does not state who imposed it. Do not infer the issuer. Note the legal framework in force on 15 December 2019 was the CrPC; BNSS did not yet exist.

title: On 19 December 2019 the Allahabad High Court (Chief Justice Govind Mathur and Justice Vivek Varma) in a PIL by Mohd. Aman Khan issued notice to the Uttar Prades
establishes: Case: Mohd. Aman Khan v. Union of India, Criminal Misc. PIL No. 26085 of 2019 (SCC Online cite 2019 SCC OnLine All 5343). The order PDF is linked by The Leaflet at cdn.theleaflet.in; the host did not resolve from this environment, so the order itself was NOT read. Upgrade to VERIFIED needs the order text from the High Court or a legal database.

title: On 7 January 2020 the Allahabad High Court asked the National Human Rights Commission to inquire into the alleged police violence at AMU and report preferably w
establishes: Order not read; three reports agree. Counter affidavit placed on record with compact discs of video; the court said it had not examined the footage. SCC Online notes the NHRC was already inquiring into Jamia Millia Islamia complaints. Senior Advocate Colin Gonsalves argued for a fuller investigation than an NHRC inquiry (SCC summary).

title: On 24 February 2020 the Allahabad High Court, recording the NHRC's report, directed the Chief Secretary of Uttar Pradesh to provide suitable compensation to six
establishes: The NHRC report itself and the 24 February order were not read. As reported, NHRC recommendations address the DGP, DG CRPF, Chief Secretary and AMU's Vice Chancellor and Registrar; none of the reports read says the NHRC identified who authorised entry. SCC Online Times states: DM and SSP not mentioned; who called police not stated. The 'attacked unnecessarily' phrasing is from a secondary summary of the NHRC report and is not quoted from the report. The reference to a State SIT set up by the DGP's order of 6 January 2020 is as reported by SCC Online Times. Outcome after 25 March 2020 not found.

title: The NHRC findings, as reported, do not state who gave the order for police entry, for use of force, for the internet suspension or for Section 144. The orders a
establishes: This is a record of absence in secondary summaries. The NHRC report itself was not obtained. A magisterial inquiry may exist and was not found; absence of a hit is not proof. Next steps: RTI to NHRC for its report (case reference from the High Court order); RTI to the District Magistrate and Home Department UP for any inquiry notification, the Section 144 order and the internet suspension order.

title: The Registrar of AMU is described in the Karwan e Mohabbat fact-finding report as a serving Uttar Pradesh police officer on deputation. The report also says the
establishes: Single source, an advocacy fact-finding team whose visit was on 17 December 2019 (members listed on the page include Harsh Mander, Nandini Sundar, John Dayal). The report's footnote says responsibility for errors lies with Harsh Mander. Allegations as the report made them; not tested. The Registrar's name (Abdul Hamid) appeared only in a search summary and is not confirmed from a fetched page. Relevance to the chain of orders: it records that the person who, per the State's affidavit, asked the DM for security was a police officer on deputation. That is the report's statement; no source for it was shown on the page.

title: Statements on stone pelting: the SSP of Aligarh, Akash Kulhari, alleged students pelted security forces with stones, injuring policemen and RAF personnel; polic
establishes: Conflict on tear gas: The Quint says police denied using tear gas shells; Sabrang reports the State's counter affidavit says water cannon and tear gas were used. Both versions are as reported; the affidavit text was not seen. Karwan e Mohabbat report says the Registrar confirmed use of stun grenades, tear gas and water cannons. Allegations by students are attributed to them.

title: On 5 January 2020 a group of masked people armed with sticks and rods entered the Jawaharlal Nehru University campus, New Delhi, and attacked students and teach
establishes: Occurrence corroborated. Duration differs by source (nearly two hours in the Tribune report of 6 January 2020, three hours in NDTV's). No finding on who the attackers were; attributions in the press are allegations by students, the ABVP and others and are not recorded here.

title: Injury count on 5 January 2020 differs by source: at least 34 (NDTV, 6 January 2020); about 35 (ETV Bharat, 9 January 2020); at least 32 students (Al Jazeera, 7
establishes: Both versions kept. The 51 figure rests on a ministerial reply the archive has not read. Ask for the Lok Sabha question and answer text on sansad.in to settle which count the Government gave and on which date. The counts may measure different things (admitted to hospital, medically examined, treated and discharged).

title: A Delhi Police spokesperson, Mandeep Singh Randhawa, said on 6 January 2020 that police 'can go to this area only with a written permission from the JNU adminis
establishes: This is the police account, attributed to the force's spokesperson at office level. Contested by the VC's statement in HIST-JNU20-006. The Times of India article was retrieved through a scraping service; the page and quotes were read in full. No police order, GD entry or the registrar's letter has been seen.

title: A Delhi Police fact-finding committee headed by the Joint Commissioner of Police (Western Range), Shalini Singh, set up on the orders of the then Police Commiss
establishes: One origin (the Indian Express, which the archive has not retrieved), relayed by two outlets, so REPORTED and not CORROBORATED. Named officials appear because the relayed report names them as witnesses to the committee. The report itself is not public so far as the archive knows. File an RTI for it. The committee was a self-review by the force and its clean chit is an internal finding.

title: A Delhi Police spokesperson rejected allegations that police reached the campus late, saying on 6 January 2020: 'We have responded to PCR calls, and law-and-ord
establishes: Single source. Names the spokesperson as the article does. The article gives no arrival times.

title: The timing and authority for police entry is DISPUTED. The Vice-Chancellor's press release of 5 January 2020 said the administration called police at about 4.30
establishes: Both versions kept, with no attempt to choose. Times: police 7 pm at admin block or gates, 7.45 pm written permission; National Herald: about 9 pm entry; VC: called at about 4.30 pm. The Congress report is a party document and its characterisation of the Vice-Chancellor is its own allegation. Neither the VC press release nor the registrar's letter was seen. Documents that would settle it: the registrar's letter, the VC's WhatsApp message, the PCR log, the control-room and GD entries for Vasant Kunj (North).

title: The Times of India reported on 7 January 2020 that police officials said they were treading with caution after the Jamia protests, and that 'Many men from the j
establishes: Single source, anonymous police sources. The 'asked to avoid confrontation and wait for orders' line is an unattributed report of constables' accounts, the nearest thing in the record to an instruction, and it names no issuing office. Treat as UNVERIFIED at the level of any specific order.

title: In a written Rajya Sabha reply reported on 18 March 2020, the Minister of State for Home Affairs, G. Kishan Reddy, said per Delhi Police that the North Gate was
establishes: This is the Union Home Ministry relaying the Delhi Police account in Parliament. It says the Vice-Chancellor requested help, which bears on who held the authority to call police in. It does not give a time. Locate the answer on sansad.in to move this to VERIFIED. Other reporting alleges violence and assault outside the North Gate (journalists, Yogendra Yadav); that conflict is not resolved here.

title: On 3 August 2021 the Minister of State for Home, Nityanand Rai, in a written Lok Sabha reply to Dayanidhi Maran, said as reported by Delhi Police that no arrest
establishes: Two outlets agree on one parliamentary reply, so this corroborates the reporting. The reply text was not retrieved. Note a discrepancy reported by SabrangIndia: Delhi Police had spoken of four FIRs, the reply says three cases.

title: Delhi Police registered a case on 6 January 2020 at Vasant Kunj (North) police station on the 5 January violence, under sections reported as rioting and damagin
establishes: FIR number not found in any source read. Times of India says the FIR states violence began around 3.45 pm and that the complainant inspector describes 40 to 50 masked persons at Periyar Hostel who ran when police arrived. That description is the FIR content as reported and remains unproven. National Herald a month later reported complainants saying no FIR on their complaints had been registered; these accounts conflict about whether the 6 January case counts as the FIR on the teachers' and students' complaints. Obtain the FIR text from the Delhi Police e-FIR portal or by RTI.

title: The FIR on Prof. Sucharita Sen's complaint, as recorded before the Duty Metropolitan Magistrate at Patiala House Courts (reported May 2020), was registered at V
establishes: Two outlets on one order. The order date is not given in either; LiveLaw published on 6 May 2020. The statute named 'DPDP Act' is quoted as the outlets wrote it and is presumably the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, which neither says; do not expand it without the order. National Herald's separate report says a magistrate sought an action taken report on 3 February 2020, returnable 25 March 2020 (Metropolitan Magistrate Ankita Lal, per that article). Two orders are therefore reported, and the archive has seen neither.

title: Separate FIRs against students: a Delhi Police case was filed against the JNU Students' Union president and 19 others over vandalism of a server room on 4 Janua
establishes: These are police allegations and complaints, which establish no guilt. The Quint article says Tirkey named nine students and did not specify two of their affiliations. Wikipedia's FIR timing is a lead only; no primary source was read for it. The DCP Crime Branch is named because the article names him as the speaker at the briefing.

title: On 13 January 2020 Justice Brijesh Sethi of the Delhi High Court issued notices to Google, WhatsApp and Apple on a petition by three JNU professors (Ameet Param
establishes: Single outlet read. The order was not retrieved. Case number not found. The date of 13 January is inferred from the article's reference to Monday and not confirmed by a second page read.

title: On 14 January 2020 the Delhi High Court (Justice Brijesh Sethi) directed Delhi Police to summon the members of the two WhatsApp groups and seize their phones, a
establishes: Two outlets on one hearing. The order text was not retrieved from the Delhi High Court or Indian Kanoon; a search of Indian Kanoon found nothing. Petition and case number not found. The order is a direction on evidence preservation and makes no finding on police conduct.

title: Records of what Delhi Police and JNU said to the Delhi High Court about CCTV: police said in January 2020 they had asked the university for CCTV and had not rec
establishes: The RTI replies are cited only through Wikipedia and are not confirmed. The Wire, News18 and NDTV articles that Wikipedia cites were not read (The Wire page returned headline only; NDTV and News18 not fetched). The gate footage question bears directly on who was at the gates.

title: JNU's Vice-Chancellor M. Jagadesh Kumar announced a five-member committee to probe the 5 January violence, recommend safety measures and examine lapses. Members
establishes: Single source, 9 January 2020. A Deccan Herald item listed in search results said the probe was delayed by COVID-19, but that page returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so no delay is recorded. Findings of this committee: not found.

title: A Delhi Police fact-finding committee headed by JCP (Western Range) Shalini Singh was set up on 6 January 2020 to examine the police response, in addition to th
establishes: Formation is reported by the Tribune; the clean chit is one Indian Express origin. The committee is internal to the force. The Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative argued such inquiries lack legitimacy for this task and called for a judicial inquiry (HIST-JNU20-019).

title: The Congress fact-finding committee report (Sushmita Dev, Syed Nasir Hussain, Hibi Eden, Amrita Dhawan), dated 13 January 2020 in the source, alleges that the V
establishes: This is an allegation by a political party's committee. The archive makes no finding on it. The Vice-Chancellor's reply to the specific allegation was not found.

title: The Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative published a press release calling for an independent judicial inquiry into police 'inaction' at JNU, alleging police st
establishes: An advocacy organisation's demand and allegation. The page prints the date as 9 January 2019, which is evidently a typing error for 2020 since the text refers to events of January 2020 and December 2019. It records no order and no response from any office.

title: Delhi Police senior officials said they had written at least four letters to the JNU registrar between November and December 2019 urging dialogue with the Stude
establishes: Single source, anonymous. It shows police already had a working channel to the registrar, relevant to who communicated with whom. The letters were not seen.

title: On 5 January 2020 the Delhi Police presence on campus before the attack: Delhi Police said a team including an inspector was deployed at the administrative bloc
establishes: Two outlets agree that police were at the administrative block under a court order, but the 27-personnel figure comes from only one. NDTV quotes the JNUSU Vice President, Saket Moon, saying 'The police had been in the campus since afternoon, but they did nothing.' That is an allegation and is not recorded as established.

title: Who gave the order that police would or would not enter the JNU campus, or hold at the gates, on 5 January 2020: no order, written or oral, and no named person
establishes: UNKNOWN is the correct state. Not established: who decided that police would wait; whether any police officer (DCP South-West, SHO, Commissioner) issued an instruction to hold; whether the Ministry of Home Affairs, which oversees Delhi Police, was consulted before the attack (the Times of India reports the Union Home Minister asked for a report on 6 January 2020, after the attack); the content of the VC's WhatsApp message and the Registrar's letter; and the legal position that a university's consent is required before police enter, which a lawyer should confirm against current law.

title: Whether a charge sheet has been filed against anyone in the Crime Branch investigation into the 5 January 2020 JNU violence, and the current status of the three
establishes: Searches for later coverage and court records found nothing after mid-2020 other than the 2021 reply. File an RTI with the Crime Branch and check the Patiala House eCourts record.

title: On 27 August 2024 a march called the Nabanna Abhijan, organised by the student group Paschim Banga Chhatra Samaj and the state employees' platform Sangrami Jout
establishes: Occurrence and route corroborated by several outlets (PTI, Business Today, All India Radio). No finding on conduct or proportionality.

title: Police used lathicharge, water cannon and tear gas against marchers on 27 August 2024, at locations reported as MG Road, Hastings Road, near Princep Ghat, Howra
establishes: Use of the three means is reported by PTI, IANS, All India Radio and Republic World. None of the pages read says which officer authorised any of them.

title: Police said they began lathicharge and tear gas after marchers breached barricades at some locations and attacked security personnel; marchers said police actio
establishes: DISPUTED. Police version: barricades breached, personnel attacked, bricks and stones thrown, 'Police said' (unnamed). Protesters' version: a rally that broke no law (an unnamed woman marcher: 'Why were we beaten by police? We did not break any law.'). No footage or document read that settles it.

title: ADG (Law and Order) Manoj Verma stated on 26 August 2024, as reported, that no individual or organisation had applied for permission, that the police learned of
establishes: Attributed to the ADG (Law and Order), West Bengal Police, as reported. Statement made before the march. The reports do not say which office issued the Section 163 order.

title: WHO ISSUED THE SECTION 163 BNSS PROHIBITORY ORDER NEAR NABANNA: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports attribute it variously to 'the government' (Tribune, Business Today, ET
establishes: Section 163 BNSS orders are made by authorised executive magistrates, which is a statutory point to be checked against the current text and implies nothing about this order. Nabanna is in Howrah district, so the Howrah Police Commissionerate area is the likelier jurisdiction, but that is inference and no document was read. Lawful routes: RTI to the Howrah Police Commissionerate and Kolkata Police, and to the Home and Hill Affairs Department, asking for the order, its date and the issuing authority; the same question at each office.

title: ADG (South Bengal) Supratim Sarkar said police had rejected applications from both organisations, which arrived late; that the Chhatra Samaj email was an intima
establishes: DISPUTED between the ADG (South Bengal), who says no valid application, and the organisers' spokesperson, who says police were informed. The Orissa Post report has the ADG saying permission was denied to both organisations; ETV Bharat has him saying applications were rejected. No application or rejection letter was found.

title: On 23 August 2024 a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court (Harish Tandon and Hiranmay Bhattacharyya JJ.), in the public interest petition WPA(P) 360 of 2024
establishes: Corrected 10 October 2026 against the order itself (HIST-CRT-004). An earlier version of this item, built on a news report, said the court refused the State's plea for a ban. The order shows the petitioner was a private litigant who sought the ban and that the State argued against the rally. Single report read (IANS via Sakshi Post). Second judge's name inconsistent across search snippets. Order text not read. Directly bears on the 'permission' question: the court declined to ban, which is not the same as granting permission. Primary source: Calcutta High Court order of 23 August 2024, to be obtained via the High Court website or Indian Kanoon.

title: Barricading: reports say police put up aluminium guard walls with wooden barricades at at least five Kolkata approach points including the foot of Howrah Bridge
establishes: Descriptions differ in detail and none names who ordered the barricading. A BJP leader, Amit Malviya, alleged the Chief Minister ordered the containers placed; that is an allegation by a party spokesperson reported by Business Today, with no document behind it.

title: Deployment as reported before the march: Tribune reports at least 25 DCP-ranked officers in Kolkata Police jurisdiction and over 2,000 personnel at Howrah appro
establishes: Figures differ between the two reports (the Tribune headline says 6,000 but its body does not give the figure). Neither names who ordered the deployment. Deployment orders are not public; see HIST-NAB-020.

title: Injured, as reported: PTI via The Hitavada says police told reporters 15 Kolkata Police personnel and 14 state police personnel were injured; protesters were al
establishes: Police injury figure is from police, unattributed to a named officer, one outlet. No count of injured protesters found from any official source. The NHRC complaint wording is the complainant's unproven allegation.

title: Arrests and detentions, as reported: IANS and Morung Express report 220 arrests in connection with the clashes plus 25 preventive arrests before the march. Hita
establishes: DISPUTED on the count: 220 plus 25 preventive (245 in total) is consistent with ETV Bharat's 245 but the sources do not say which police force made which arrests. No FIR numbers or arrest memos found.

title: Four persons (named in reports as Subhojit Ghosh, Pulokesh Pandit, Goutam Senapati and Pritam Sarkar) were reported missing before the march. West Bengal Police
establishes: Attributed: Adhikari's statement and the police statement are as reported by Orissa Post. Names are as reported and are not independently confirmed. The police allegation of conspiracy is an unproven allegation.

title: On 2 September 2024 Justice Rajarshi Bharadwaj of the Calcutta High Court, hearing the petition on the four persons, asked the State to produce the relevant doc
establishes: The Orissa Post page confirms Adhikari petitioned and Justice Rajarshi Bharadwaj allowed the petition to be filed; the details of the 2 September hearing, including the State's statement that Howrah city police made preventive arrests, come from a search result summary of a Deccan Herald page that returned HTTP 403, so were NOT read. Do not promote until the Deccan Herald page or the order is read. The attribution to Howrah city police would be the clearest office-level statement on who made the preventive arrests.

title: On 30 August 2024 Justice Amrita Sinha of the Calcutta High Court directed Kolkata Police to release Sayan Lahiri, a Nabanna Abhijan convenor, and ordered no co
establishes: Two independent reports (IANS; LawTrend). FIR number, sections and the arrest authority's rank not stated in either. The State was directed to file an affidavit in opposition by 20 September 2024 and the petitioner a reply by 4 October 2024 (LawTrend). Order text not read.

title: Whether the State of West Bengal challenged the Calcutta High Court's order in the Sayan Lahiri matter before the Supreme Court, and with what result, is not es
establishes: A headline seen only as a search result suggests the Supreme Court dismissed such a plea on 2 September 2024. No page and no order was read, so it is not recorded as a fact. A Bar & Bench page about a Supreme Court rebuke to West Bengal over a bail challenge concerns a different case (State of West Bengal v. Rajdeep Roy) and must not be used here. Obtain the order from the Supreme Court website.

title: The NHRC issued a notice to the Commissioner of Police, Kolkata, on or about 29 August 2024, as reported on 30 and 31 August 2024, seeking an action taken repor
establishes: Two reports read. Exact notice date not stated: 'Thursday' (ETV Bharat, i.e. likely 29 August 2024) while IANS dated its story 30 August. The complaint is the complainant's allegation. Kolkata Police reply not found. NHRC case number not found.

title: Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, speaking at the 27th Foundation Day of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad, as quoted by Swarajya on 28 August 2024: 'We
establishes: Single report. The quote is attributed to the Chief Minister by the outlet; no recording or transcript read. This is a post-hoc endorsement and not evidence that she gave an order. The Trinamool Congress called the rally a 'conspiracy' to create public disorder (Tribune).

title: Opposition and BJP statements as reported: BJP's Amit Malviya alleged the Chief Minister ordered police to place containers on the road to stop protesters; BJP
establishes: All allegations by named party figures, reported by Business Today and LiveLaw. No document supports the claim that the Chief Minister gave an order about containers. Governor CV Ananda Bose urged the state not to use force (Tribune, News On AIR, paraphrased). Quote check, 10 October 2026: neither cited page gives the bandh date, so the date was removed.

title: WHO GAVE THE ORDER for tear gas, water cannon and lathicharge on 27 August 2024: NOT ESTABLISHED. Every report read says police used them and records police say
establishes: BT states in its own words that the article does not name who ordered the tear gas, lathicharge and water cannon. Onmanorama and Tribune likewise. No Commissioner of Police for either city was quoted on record in any page read; do not name an individual. Lawful routes: RTI for the control-room log and the dispersal order at both commissionerates; BNSS dispersal provisions to be verified against current text; the State's affidavit in the Lahiri matter and the answer to the NHRC notice.

title: Documents that would settle the order question and were not found or read: the Section 163 BNSS order (issuer, date, area); the deployment order and requisition
establishes: None obtained. No RTI is on record in this archive for this incident. Treat as the filing list.

title: Kolkata Police entered the Jadavpur University campus in the early hours of 17 September 2014 (about 2:00 a.m. per one report) to end a students' sit-in or gher
establishes: Four news outlets agree on the occurrence. None is a primary document. Time of entry: DNA says about 2:00 a.m.; Gulf News (PTI) says 'early hours of Wednesday'. Wikipedia (not relied on) says police arrived about 8 p.m. on 16 September and the action came about 2 a.m. No finding on the lawfulness or proportionality of the entry or of any force. Incident id left blank for the editor to assign.

title: Who requisitioned the police. The interim Vice-Chancellor of Jadavpur University is reported by DNA to have said he was 'forced to call the police' after demons
establishes: Office-level only: the interim Vice-Chancellor. No order, requisition letter, FIR, affidavit or inquiry report naming the person or recording the request was read. The DNA article, in one place, gives the VC a wrong surname, so it is treated with care; the statement that the VC said he was forced to call police is the DNA reporter's account of his words. See HIST-JU14-003 for the conflicting later statements.

title: Conflict over whether the Vice-Chancellor took the decision to call police onto campus. (a) DNA, Global Voices and the students: the VC called the police. (b) T
establishes: Version (b) is not necessarily a denial of 16 and 17 September: the quoted sentence is undated and its context in the article is not given beyond the sentence. It is recorded as a conflict because on its face it sits against (a). Version (c) rests only on Wikipedia, whose cited Hindu article could not be fetched. Version (d) is an advocacy petition. Not resolved. What would resolve it: the written requisition or the police station diary entry recording who asked for entry, the Executive Council minutes, and any affidavit.

title: Which office authorised or directed the specific use of force inside the campus (lights switched off, alleged baton blows, arrests) is not established by any do
establishes: A commissioner-level or additional-commissioner-level operational order, the deployment order, and the station diary are the missing records. DNA (HIST-JU14-006) names an Additional Commissioner of Police as leading the contingent; that is a report of presence only.

title: Whether the state government or a minister gave any direction for the police action. The Change.org petition alleges the state government gave a 'green signal'.
establishes: Allegation by the petitioners, unsupported by a document. The Minister's quote shows a public position after the event. Office-level only: Education Minister, Government of West Bengal.

title: DNA reported that an Additional Commissioner of Police led a strong contingent to the campus at about 2:00 a.m. on 17 September 2014.
establishes: Single source. The article gives a named officer; the name is not repeated here because no primary document read names that person. Record at the level of office: an Additional Commissioner of Police, Kolkata Police.

title: Police and some media accounts held that only minimal force was used. Wikipedia reports the Kolkata Police position as 'minimum lawful force' to escort the Vice
establishes: Police position is cited only through Wikipedia (tertiary); the original Kolkata Police Facebook post and Times of India article it cites could not be read. The allegations are the students' and petitioners' own, and Global Voices reports 'allegations that some activists from the Trinamool Chhatra Parishad also aided the police'. No finding on force, intent or identity of any person in plain clothes. Kafila carries a reader comment that lights went off at 2 to 2:30 on 17 September; that is one commenter's claim.

title: Arrests on the night of 16 to 17 September 2014: the count is reported as 35 (Gulf News/PTI, released on personal bonds), 36 (Global Voices; the petition says 3
establishes: Counts differ between and inside sources. No arrest memo, FIR or court remand order was read, so the true figure and the sections charged are not established. Gulf News adds that police said the blockade at Jadavpur Police Station was lifted on the condition of an independent probe into the alleged harassment.

title: Injuries on 17 September 2014. DNA reports that a couple of students were in critical condition, one in the ICU of a nearby hospital and another needing surgery
establishes: No hospital record, medico-legal certificate or official count was read. The 40 figure is unsourced and should not be repeated. Medico-legal records need the consent of the persons concerned.

title: The molestation complaint behind the protest reached police in early September 2014: a student's father lodged a police complaint with police (2 September 2014)
establishes: Dates rest on Wikipedia alone; its cited Times of India, Telegraph and Ei Samay pieces were not fetched. The existence of a molestation complaint as the cause of the protest is reported by the other sources in HIST-JU14-001 without those dates. Records to request: the FIR or complaint registered, the general diary entry, and the case file status.

title: Whether a public interest litigation was filed in the Calcutta High Court over the police action, and what the court ordered.
establishes: A model-written summary (Grokipedia, not cited as a source) listed an India Today article about a PIL and an order for affidavits on 19 September 2014. India Today could not be fetched (blocked), the claim was not independently found, and a search of the Calcutta High Court coverage found only unrelated later cases (2023 and 2025). Treat as a lead to check on the court's case status portal and Indian Kanoon.

title: Whether the West Bengal government constituted a panel to look into the police action, and whether any inquiry report on the 16 and 17 September events was publ
establishes: The same unreliable summary lists a five-member state panel and a government pledge of an inquiry on 21 September 2014, citing Business Standard and BBC pages that were blocked. A search snippet also mentions a university committee on the unrest and the role of police. None was read. Wikipedia (read) states no inquiry findings are reported. Records to request: the notification constituting any panel, its terms of reference and report, from the West Bengal Home Department and the university.

title: Outcome for the Vice-Chancellor: The News Minute reported on 14 January 2015 that the Vice-Chancellor announced his resignation on Monday 12 January 2015, calli
establishes: Single source read. Wikipedia says the Chief Minister announced the resignation after a student hunger strike; that is not verified here. No finding follows from the resignation about who ordered anything on 17 September.

title: No criminal case, departmental action or court finding against any police officer or university official for the events of 17 September 2014 was found in the so
establishes: This records the absence of what was found and says nothing about whether any exists. Check: eCourts and the Calcutta High Court cause lists for 2014 and 2015, the West Bengal Human Rights Commission, the National Human Rights Commission case search, and RTI to Kolkata Police.

title: Students of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, boycotted classes from 12 June 2015 in a strike against the appointment of Gajendra Chauhan
establishes: The strike is the context for every police action recorded here. The two outlets both carry agency copy (PTI) and may share a wire origin, so the two are not independent and the item stays at REPORTED. Whether the strike ended on 28 October 2015 (139 days) is reported by The Quint only as a duration; the end date was not read in a fetched page.

title: Pune Police entered the FTII campus after midnight on the night of 18 to 19 August 2015 and arrested five students. The Tribune (PTI) and Ummid (IANS) both repo
establishes: Occurrence is corroborated by three outlets, two of them different wire agencies. One tweet by a film technician quoted in the Tribune says 40 students were arrested; the article itself reports five. No finding on the conduct or proportionality of the police action is made here.

title: Timing of the police entry is DISPUTED. The Tribune (PTI) says the director went to police at 9:30 pm on 18 August 2015 and police reached the campus about an h
establishes: The sources are all press reports; no station diary, control-room log or FIR was read. A station diary (roznamcha) entry or the control-room log would fix the time.

title: Who gave the order for police to enter the FTII campus and arrest students on the night of 18 to 19 August 2015: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports say the director, Pras
establishes: At the level of office, the reports point to two actors whose roles are described differently: the institute's director (complainant, and by his own account the person who called the police) and Pune Police (registered the FIR, sent the teams). Which police office authorised an operation after midnight, and whether a magistrate's warrant was involved, is not stated in any source read. The Wire says neither the director nor the registrar was on campus when the arrests were made. Attributing the order to anyone would go beyond the documents.

title: Whether the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting directed the institute's director or Pune Police to call the police or make arrests: NOT ESTABLISHED. Free
establishes: The denial is the director's statement as reported, and the students' motive claim is an allegation. Neither is a document. Ummid (IANS, 21 August 2015) also reports that police and private security were deployed on campus and were removed on Friday 21 August; the order for that deployment is not stated.

title: The FIR on the director's complaint: The Tribune (PTI) quotes DCP T Tushar Doshi as saying 'FIRs have been filed against 15 students out of which five have been
establishes: Conflict is on the number of accused: 15 named (Tribune, FPJ, Ummid) against 40 in total with 15 named (The Wire). Ummid separately says police were searching for about 40 students who had confronted the director. The FIR itself was not read. On 11 March 2016 Inspector Pravin Chaugule of Deccan Gymkhana Police is quoted by PTI as saying 17 students were 'already identified and named in the earlier FIR', which differs again from 15.

title: The FIR was reported to include Indian Penal Code sections 143, 147, 149, 323, 353 and 506 'etc.', described as covering unlawful assembly, rioting and criminal
establishes: Single source, and the section list is the newspaper's; the FIR itself was not read for it. Other outlets say only 'rioting' and 'illegal confinement' without section numbers. Allegations are the complainant's; no court has been found to have made findings on them.

title: The five arrested students were produced before a Pune magistrate on 19 August 2015 and were released on bail the same day. Ummid (IANS) reports they were reman
establishes: The bail amount and the lawyers' names rest on Ummid alone. The Wire names no court and gives no amount. No bail order was read. Ummid also reports that at least another dozen students sought anticipatory bail.

title: On 11 March 2016 PTI reported that police had named 18 more FTII students in the gherao case, bringing the total named to 35. Of the 17 earlier named, five were
establishes: Single source read. The Wire carries an article titled 'FTII struggle continues as police serves fresh notices' but its body could not be read, so it is not cited. The outcome of the 14 March 2016 date, any charge sheet and the final result of the case were not found (see HIST-FTII-016).

title: Whether the students confined and harassed the director on 17 August 2015 is DISPUTED. The director, Prashant Pathrabe, says he was held in 'illegal confinement
establishes: These are allegations by named parties and are not findings. Ummid (IANS) reports a police officer alleged that students blocked people from leaving, cut telephone lines and damaged computers. No video was examined. The Gulf News page carries a 2018 date stamp but its body is August 2015 reporting.

title: Injuries and force in the August 2015 campus operation: no injury count and no report of baton use were found in the sources read. Gulf News (IANS) quotes the d
establishes: Absence in the sources read is not a finding that no one was hurt. Medical records and the arrest memos would settle this and could be requested (see notes file).

title: An Information and Broadcasting Ministry panel report on the FTII situation, reported by the press to say that the director was entitled to call the police and
establishes: A search result summary attributed the report to the Khan panel and to an RTI activist, Vijay Kumbhar, but a search summary is not a source. If obtained, the report is a primary document on whether the ministry endorsed the police call after the event. It does not show who authorised the entry.

title: On 3 July 2015 police detained students protesting outside the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at Shastri Bhavan, New Delhi, against Gajendra Chauhan's
establishes: Moneylife names Delhi Police; The Tribune does not name the force and quotes the students' association as saying the protest was disrupted by 'police and CRPF'. Gulf Times refers to the detentions as happening 'yesterday' while carrying a 3 July dateline, so its date is uncertain. Delhi Police reports to the Ministry of Home Affairs and has no reporting line to the Delhi government.

title: Who ordered the detentions at Shastri Bhavan on 3 July 2015: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Tribune quotes an unnamed official: 'This is to ensure that the protest does n
establishes: The quote is attributed to 'an official' with no designation. No Delhi Police order, deployment record or request from the ministry to police was found. A request by the ministry to Delhi Police, if one exists, is a document that could be asked for under RTI.

title: A further Delhi protest outside Shastri Bhavan, said to have led to 12 students being detained, was mentioned in a search result attributed to a HuffPost India
establishes: Treat as a lead only. The Deccan Herald piece titled as the students' body alleging police high-handedness during a Delhi protest returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

title: Final outcome of the criminal case arising from the 17 August 2015 gherao (charge sheet, trial, withdrawal, discharge or acquittal): not found in any source rea
establishes: The case would be before a Pune magistrate's court; the case number and court were not found. The ministry panel is reported to have said the matter was before a court.

title: On 7 January 2016, when Gajendra Chauhan formally took charge as chairman, Pune Police detained FTII students protesting outside the campus and used force. The
establishes: This is after the student strike was reported to have been called off, so whether it belongs to the 2015 strike or to the continuing dispute over the appointment is a matter of scope for the archive. The Logical Indian says 17 students had been served notices warning bail could be cancelled; Assam Tribune says at least 17 were served notices beforehand. The DCP is named 'Tushar Doshi' in August 2015 reports (Tribune, FPJ) and 'Tushar Joshi' in January 2016 reports; the sources do not say whether this is one officer with a spelling variant. No injury count was found.

title: Who gave the order to use force and detain students on 7 January 2016: NOT ESTABLISHED. Deputy Commissioner of Police Tushar Joshi, Pune, is reported as defendi
establishes: The Logical Indian also quotes Chauhan saying 'I have been ordered by the government, and I will do my job'; this concerns his taking up the post and says nothing about police orders. Recording the DCP by name is limited to the press quotes above.

title: A Supreme Court public interest petition by advocate Vineet Dhanda was reported on 2 September 2015 asking the Court to intervene in the standoff between the Ce
establishes: Single source, partly paywalled. The petition concerns the appointment and the strike only. No order was read.

title: Students from Delhi universities began an 'Occupy UGC' protest outside the University Grants Commission office in New Delhi on 21 October 2015, after the UGC's
establishes: Two accounts written independently of each other agree on the start date, and the PUDR statement agrees. Two of the three are written by people in the protest. The Wire and Kafila place the office 'near ITO'; no source read gives the street name Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, so that detail is not carried here. Non-NET fellowships were Rs 8,000 a month for PhD and Rs 5,000 for MPhil students (The Wire).

title: Police took roughly 100 protesting students from the UGC office to Bhalswa (Bhalaswa Dairy) police station. The date and the count are DISPUTED. PUDR (2 Novembe
establishes: The incident as described to the archive ('detentions on 21 October') is not confirmed as stated. PUDR's 4:30 am on 21 October sits before the afternoon start of the occupation reported by the AISA leader and The Wire, so that time looks mistaken, but no document settles it. The 22 or 23 October dating is more consistent with the AISA account, the Amar Ujala report of a lathi charge on 23 October, and the Delhi Solidarity Group. No police record, FIR or official detainee list was found. All four sources are protest-side or advocacy accounts or quote protest participants; no police account of this detention was found.

title: Police used lathis on students sitting outside UGC gate number two on 23 October 2015, according to Amar Ujala, which says several students and police personnel
establishes: Amar Ujala is a mainstream newspaper gallery caption; it gives no injury count and names no officer. No police version of 23 October was found. The stone-throwing and bus claim is the newspaper's and is not corroborated elsewhere in the sources read.

title: On 27 October 2015 police at the UGC office lathicharged and detained protesters and took them to Kamla Market police station. Counts conflict. JNUSU's presiden
establishes: Whether a lathicharge happened is disputed: the police version, as relayed second-hand, denies it, while the protest-side sources say it happened and that mobile video shows it. PUDR says detainees were released after pressure from teachers and students and that injured students reached LNJP Hospital 'only after much pressure'. The video itself was not seen. A Deccan Herald archive report with an injury figure appeared in search results but returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The Indian Express original was not accessible.

title: The deputy commissioner of police (Central) of Delhi Police publicly said that no one had been lathicharged at the 27 October 2015 protest and that protesters h
establishes: This is a public statement after the event. Both secondary sources name the officer; the name is left out here because no primary document names him. The Kafila post gives the quote second-hand from an Indian Express report that was not read; PUDR paraphrases it. The Kafila author calls the statement false on the strength of video footage by a photojournalist. No finding is made here on either side.

title: From the first days the UGC office was under heavy police presence. An AISA leader describes a 'state of near siege' on 21 and 22 October 2015. JNUSU's presiden
establishes: Both are participant accounts. No order, notification or deployment record was found for the cordon, and no document says which office directed it.

title: On 26 October 2015 the Ministry of Human Resource Development issued an order stating that non-NET fellowships would continue for the moment and that a review c
establishes: Outcome of the policy demand only. The orders themselves were not read. The dates differ in how the two sources frame the sequence, and the HRD Minister's earlier tweet of 26 October is described by The Wire.

title: On 9 December 2015 students marching from the UGC protest toward Parliament were stopped near Feroz Shah Road. Police used lathis, water cannon and tear gas, an
establishes: Four outlets agree the force and detentions happened. The count of 150 appears only in The News Minute. Caravan puts the number of marchers at over 300 and says detainees were held at or near Parliament Street; Sabrang says three buses took students to Parliament Street police station. title: The reasons for force on 9 December 2015 are DISPUTED. The Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi) said force was used to stop a march toward Parliament, that

Delhi Police reports to the Ministry of Home Affairs, which is the route for an RTI. Do not name any individual as the giver of an order on this record.

title: Who gave the order for the 9 December 2015 force and detentions is not established. The deputy commissioner of police (New Delhi) publicly defended the use of f
establishes: Defending a decision after the event is not evidence of who gave the order. See HIST-UGC-009 and HIST-UGC-010 for the two public statements.

establishes: The letter is a complaint. The document proves what PUDR asked for; it does not prove the allegations. The letter names police personnel; those names were not checked against any record and are not repeated here. Any reply from the Commission is not known.

establishes: This is an absence in what could be searched online, which is limited. Court and FIR records would be found by direct request. Not finding a case is not evidence that none exists. Conversely, no source read says police registered an FIR against protesters.

establishes: Occurrence of force corroborated by three secondary outlets plus a tertiary summary. The reports are not independent of each other on detail: Gulf News carries a PTI account and the Tribune item is an agency dateline. No finding on proportionality, provocation or lawfulness. Police and protester accounts differ on whether tear gas was fired (a protester says yes, police say 'mild force'); the Tribune says tear gas shells were fired.

title: Many of the Marina protesters were students and young people. The Tribune report records that the 'students and youth who had called the protest' say they were
establishes: Included to fix the scope: this record is about a youth-led, student-heavy protest, and no source read gives a count of students among those removed or charged. Do not read it as a purely student event. Confidence is REPORTED because no source states the share of students.

establishes: The figures may measure different things (Marina only against statewide, injured against admitted), so they are listed side by side. Hospital admission registers and police casualty reports would settle it.

title: Number removed or detained on 23 January 2017 at Marina: NOT ESTABLISHED. Police told PTI about 7,000 protesters were present and about 2,000 remained in a huma
establishes: The 3,000 figure is relayed twice over and its date range and place are not given. It cannot be tied to Marina or to 23 January. The records that would give a count are the Chennai city police arrest and detention registers for 23 January 2017.

title: Who gave the order to clear Marina Beach on 23 January 2017, and in what form (written or oral): NOT ESTABLISHED. No document read names an officer or office as
establishes: Recorded at the level of office: the police operation in Chennai falls within the Greater Chennai Police, whose head is the Commissioner of Police (the office the High Court judgment records as issuing the later section 144 order). That is an inference about where the chain runs and establishes nothing about whether the Commissioner gave the order. The Chief Minister is reported by two outlets to have defended the operation in the Assembly (see HIST-C17A-009); a defence after the event is not an order. People's Watch states that the Commissioner declined to meet its fact-finding team; that is not an attribution of the order.

establishes: Update 10 October 2026: the 28 April 2018 judgment this item cites was set aside by a Division Bench on 3 September 2018 (W.A. 1042 of 2018; see HIST-CRT-001). The Section 144 recital here is the State's counter-affidavit account only, and the appeal judgment does not repeat it. VERIFIED only for what the judgment records the State as saying. The order itself was not read, and the paragraph gives two end dates (rescinded 4 February; ended 12 February). The order is dated five days AFTER the 23 January operation, so it is not the authority for that operation. The paragraph also records the State's account that the January 2017 gathering involved 'anti-social elements' causing 'large scale violence and damage of public property' and that a commission under Justice S. Rajeswaran (Retd.) was then in progress. Those are the State's statements and carry no finding of the court. The fetched copy was hashed at retrieval. Under CrPC as it then stood; BNSS does not apply to 2017.

establishes: The record that would answer it is the Greater Chennai Police order register and any gazette or press notice for January 2017.

establishes: Single page read. The NHRC's own release was not found. The two-week reports from the three offices, and any NHRC case number, are not public in anything read. The same report says the Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission invited complaints through a named Registrar (Law).

title: The Chief Minister is reported by two outlets (Hindustan Times, Delhi edition, and Oman Daily Observer, both via PressReader) to have told the Assembly on or ab
establishes: Encountered in search listings only. The primary record would be the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly proceedings for that week.

establishes: VERIFIED for the existence of the commission and its head, from the judgment. The terms of reference come from the two news items; the government order creating the commission was not read.

establishes: The Federal quotes Justice Rajeswaran as saying only the government can explain why it is unpublished. DT Next said tabling was expected 'soon'; whether that happened is not established. establishes: Attributed to the commission head through a third-hand relay. The Federal (2021) records the same judge as saying he could not comment on the report. establishes: An unproven allegation by a rights organisation. Source type is secondary because it is an advocacy summary.

establishes: Routes follow SOURCING.md. None of these has been requested by this research. Whether a PIL on the eviction itself was filed in the Madras High Court was not established.

establishes: Occurrence of the disruption and cancellation is corroborated by two outlets. Who threw what is an unproven allegation made by students and reported by Newslaundry. establishes: PREMISE CHECK: the brief named the march destination as the Kamla Nagar police station. Every source read says Maurice Nagar police station, which also holds the FIR (see HIST-RAM-009). Kamla Nagar is a separate locality and no read source places the march there. The 21 February clash over the seminar invitation and the 22 February march are otherwise as described. establishes: Each version is attributed to the party that gave it. The archive makes no finding on who began the violence. Swarajya is an opinion-leaning source and is used here only to record the opposing version.

establishes: That detentions happened is corroborated. The count is not: only Newslaundry gives a figure (about 100, in narration) and the sources differ on whether those held were AISA-side marchers, ABVP members or both. See HIST-RAM-005. establishes: Conflict is between the DUSU president's statement and CPJ's account about who was on the bus, and between about 100 (Newslaundry) and a possible 40 to 50 (unread PTI line, not relied on). establishes: Counts are the claims of AISA, ABVP, police and press and none comes from medical-legal records. No MLC or hospital record was read. The Indian Express article behind the 'eight police personnel' figure was not read; it is relayed by Swarajya.

establishes: These are allegations, attributed to the journalists and to complaints reported by Governance Now. CPJ names no police officer. The Delhi Union of Journalists, per IANS, noted some officers wore no nametags (see HIST-RAM-010 sources).

establishes: This establishes only what an officer said on the record to students and the press. It is a statement by an office-holder that he did not give the order and could not name who did. It has no standing as an order or as an inquiry finding. The Asian Age quote and the IANS paraphrase come from the same event but different reporters; the Oman Observer and Peninsula pieces are the same IANS wire. The word 'lathicharge' is as used by the reporters.

establishes: Level of office: the sources establish the actors as Delhi Police personnel under the Delhi Police Commissioner, with the Special Commissioner (Law and Order), the Joint Commissioner and the DCP North all named in reporting as speaking about the events. No source says any of them gave a direction on the ground. The Delhi Union of Journalists, per IANS, said some officers wore no nametags.

title: Whether Police Headquarters ordered a 'mild lathicharge' on 22 February 2017 is not established by any page read.
establishes: A lead: a search-result summary, read on 10 October 2026, said The Indian Express relayed unnamed sources to that effect. establishes: The suspended men are not named in either source and the suspension orders were not found. establishes: The notice text and NHRC case number were not found; the NHRC's own page was not located. establishes: This proceeding concerns the slogans complaint and the FIR sought; it has no bearing on police conduct on 21 and 22 February. Court order text not read. Both articles are secondary; one is auto-generated IANS copy.

establishes: DISPUTED on the signatory: Newslaundry names DCP (Crime Branch) Madhur Verma; The Caravan names Joint CP (Crime) Praveer Ranjan, and says he did not respond to its queries. establishes: Individual medico-legal records are sensitive and should not be requested for named people. Ask for counts and dates. Any step that would expose a victim or complainant must carry exposure_risk and not be auto-executed.

establishes: None requested by this research. The university is a public authority and the police are a public authority for RTI purposes, but no filing route or office designation for Chandigarh was established here, and none is borrowed from another jurisdiction.

establishes: Four secondary reports agree on the occurrence, place and a wounded student. establishes: Versions: left arm (Scroll.in) against left hand (Careers360 via ANI; Deputy Commissioner Chinmoy Biswal is quoted by Scroll.in as saying hand); AIIMS against Holy Family Hospital as first destination (Scroll.in says the Times of India first reported Holy Family). establishes: Secondary reports say a case of attempt to murder was lodged (HIST-JMF-009); the sections are not given in any page read. A separate Delhi Police Crime Branch case file would sit with the Delhi Police. Because the accused was a minor, the Board proceedings are confidential and a request may be refused on that ground.

title: Any court proceeding about police conduct or orders on 30 January 2020 (a writ, PIL, inquiry or complaint specific to the firing): NONE FOUND. The Delhi High Co
