establishes: Searches for a petition on the firing returned only the December 2019 batch (W.P.(C) 13468/2019 and connected matters, per HIST-JMI-001). No NHRC case on the 30 January firing was found. Not finding one does not show none exists; an eCourts and NHRC case-status search by party name is the next step.

title: Outcome of the case against the juvenile and against the weapon supplier, and whether any police action followed: NOT ESTABLISHED. Scroll.in reported in July 20
establishes: No Board disposal order, acquittal, conviction or closure was read. The July 2021 Scroll.in article is the latest dated page read (see HIST-JMF-009).

title: Records that could be requested to answer the order question for 30 January 2020, none of which was seen: the Delhi Police deployment or bandobast order for the
establishes: Route: RTI to the Delhi Police and to the Ministry of Home Affairs (the ministry Delhi Police reports to), filed at both offices at once per SOURCING.md, and a Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha question to the Ministry of Home Affairs. Juvenile Board records are likely to be withheld; ask only for the existence and date of the order.

title: Aspirants for the Railway Recruitment Board Non-Technical Popular Categories (RRB NTPC) exam protested in Bihar from 24 January 2022, after the first-stage (CBT
establishes: Occurrence is consistent across independent outlets. The release date of the CBT-1 results is given as 14 January by ETV Bharat (29 January) and The Quint explainer, and as 15 January by ETV Bharat (25 January), ThePrint/PTI and The Quint. Not resolved here. The Quint (28 January) says protests reached 12 districts in two days and that around 400 students were allegedly provoked at Rajendra Nagar, per the FIR. Whether the 24 January blockade began as the district administration's release describes (afternoon, Rajendra Nagar Terminal) is taken from that release as quoted by PTI.

title: On 24 January 2022 police used force to clear the track at Rajendra Nagar Terminal, Patna. The Patna district administration's release, as quoted by PTI, descri
establishes: The use of force is acknowledged by the district administration itself. Its extent is DISPUTED in the sense that the administration says 'mild' while the outlets name tear gas, a water cannon and lathis; see HIST-RRB-003. The sources share an upstream (the administration release and agency copy), so they are not fully independent of one another.

title: The extent of force used on students at Rajendra Nagar Terminal on 24 January 2022 is DISPUTED. Version 1 (Patna district administration release, via PTI): 'mil
establishes: No injury count from any official source was found. No medical or hospital record was found. The two versions are not necessarily exclusive: 'mild' is the administration's word and the others describe the instruments.

title: The number of people injured by police action in Patna in January 2022 is not established. No official count and no hospital figure was found in the sources rea
establishes: Search turned up one snippet claiming more than two dozen students were hospitalised in Patna, with unclear attribution. The page was not fetched and is not cited. A request to the Patna district hospitals for aggregate admissions for 24 to 28 January 2022 is the route.

title: At least four people were arrested after the Rajendra Nagar Terminal protest of 24 January 2022. The Patna District Magistrate said on 27 January 2022 that four
establishes: Counts differ by date and source. The Quint (28 January) reports eight students arrested by Patna Police (see HIST-RRB-006). 'At least four' by 25 January and four per the DM on 27 January are consistent with each other.

title: The Quint (28 January 2022), citing The Indian Express and ANI, reports that Patna Police had arrested eight students. The article does not say which of the six
establishes: Single source for the figure of eight. The DM's figure of four on 27 January (HIST-RRB-005) may be an earlier count. Not reconciled.

title: A First Information Report was registered at Patrakar Nagar police station, Patna, on 27 January 2022 over the January 2022 railway-exam protests. As reported,
establishes: The FIR itself was not read; its existence and contents are known only from press reports. Counts conflict: The Quint (27 and 28 January) names six teachers in all and sixteen students; ETV Bharat (29 January) says the lead teacher was named 'along with 15 other teachers'. See HIST-RRB-008. These are allegations in a police complaint. Nothing here is a finding against any named person. Sections are as printed by The Quint and have not been checked against the FIR.

title: The number of coaching teachers named in the Patna FIR is DISPUTED. Version 1 (The Quint, 27 and 28 January 2022): the lead teacher plus five others, six in all
establishes: Version 1 is supported by two articles and an SSP statement as reported. Version 2 may be a confusion with the sixteen students. Resolving it needs the FIR copy.

title: The Patna police case rests, as reported, on statements by protesters taken into custody on 24 and 25 January 2022. The Quint (27 January) says the complaint 'w
establishes: All of these are allegations by police or by arrested people, and denials by the accused. They are recorded as attributed statements and are not findings. Statements given to police in custody are the basis of the FIR, per the press; their voluntariness is not examined in any source read. Whether any of the accused was arrested, or whether the case was later dropped, quashed or charge-sheeted, was not found (see HIST-RRB-016).

title: A Patna district administration release, as quoted by PTI on 25 January 2022, said it was 'suspected that the protesters might have been instigated by those run
establishes: This is the earliest official statement found that links the protest to coaching institutes, before the 27 January FIR. Quoted at second hand from a release; the release was not read.

title: Who ordered or authorised the use of force at Rajendra Nagar Terminal on 24 January 2022 is not established by any document read. The only account found is the
establishes: Recorded at the level of office. The press names the two officeholders; no primary document read here names them, so they are not entered as findings. The statement is the administration's description of its own conduct. Records that could settle it: deployment orders and station diary of the Patna railway police and district police for 24 January 2022, and any magisterial inquiry order.

title: Police entry into student lodges, hostels or coaching hostels in Patna during the January 2022 railway-exam protests is not established. No source read reports
establishes: The premise that lodges were entered in Patna was searched in English and Hindi and not found. The documented lodge entries are in Prayagraj (see HIST-RRB-020). Local Hindi dailies for 24 to 29 January 2022 were not searched in full and may hold reports.

title: The Ministry of Railways issued a notice on 25 January 2022 warning that candidates 'found indulging in unlawful activities' during the NTPC protests would be '
establishes: Quoted at second hand; the notice itself was not obtained (the Quint explainer says an earlier press release was removed from the official site). This is a Union ministry statement of consequences. It is not an order to any state police force, and no source links it to the Patna or Prayagraj operations. The committee date for recommendations is given as 4 March 2022 by The Quint.

title: On 26 January 2022 protesting aspirants set a train coach on fire at Gaya. ETV Bharat Hindi (26 January) also reports that a rail engine was set on fire at Nawa
establishes: Context for the police response and for the later FIR. Details of arrests in Gaya and Nawada were not found. Sitamarhi: police fired in the air to disperse a crowd, per PTI via ThePrint (25 January 2022).

title: The Indian Youth Congress said on 27 January 2022 that it had filed a complaint with the National Human Rights Commission alleging violation of the human rights
establishes: This records that a complaint was filed, as stated by the complainant. No NHRC registration number, notice, report call or outcome was found. Do not treat it as NHRC action. The NHRC case status can be requested or searched by diary number if the Indian Youth Congress will share it.

title: No Patna High Court proceeding, no NHRC or Bihar State Human Rights Commission action, no judicial or magisterial inquiry, and no suspension of any Bihar police
establishes: Absence in the sources searched is not evidence that none exists. Searches in English and Hindi for a Patna High Court matter returned only unrelated 2026 matters involving the same lead teacher. Routes: eCourts search in Patna civil and sessions court, Patna High Court case status, RTI to Patna SSP office, and to the Bihar home department for any inquiry.

title: On 25 January 2022 in Prayagraj, aspirants protesting the RRB NTPC results sat on the railway line near the station area; police dispersed them, and police ente
establishes: Five outlets, with Newslaundry reporting from lodges in Chota Baghara weeks later and Alt News using the same account (its main point is a mis-dated photo used by another paper, which it removes from the evidence). Date: the incident is 25 January 2022 (Tuesday). Deccan Herald (26 January) and India TV give the same day. The BW piece gives the location as Chota Baghada. Police wording is in HIST-RRB-019.

title: How the victims are described in the sources: Deccan Herald says 'several students' on the tracks were injured, 'some seriously', and that videos showed police
establishes: Individuals are not named here. Newslaundry also reports that many students left their rooms out of fear. No injury count, no hospital figure and no count of people detained inside lodges was found. Alt News flags one widely used injury photo as a 2019 image from elsewhere, so unverified injury photographs from 28 January coverage should not be used.

title: Police account of why they entered the lodges is DISPUTED. Version 1 (Prayagraj SSP, as reported by PTI/India TV on 27 January 2022): some of the protesters pel
establishes: Version 3 is Alt News's summary and partly agrees with each of the others. What was thrown, by whom, and who among those beaten had taken part, is not established by any document.

title: The Prayagraj SSP said at Police Lines on 26 January 2022 that a video had surfaced in which some policemen were seen using unnecessary force, that the policeme
establishes: The earlier Deccan Herald count of three is likely superseded by the later statement of six, but this has not been confirmed by a suspension order. Officers are not named here; the SSP's statement names them as reported by PTI and no suspension order was read. Whether departmental action ended in any punishment was not found. Newslaundry (10 February) states six were suspended.

title: Who gave the order for the dispersal and for entry into lodges in Prayagraj on 25 January 2022 is not established. The only on-record position found is the Pray
establishes: Recorded at the level of office: the Prayagraj district police leadership (SSP). Nothing reaches above the district in the sources read. An 11-member police team was set up, per the SSP, to investigate the alleged funding of the protest (see HIST-RRB-022). Whether an inquiry into police conduct was held and who led it was not found: Deccan Herald (26 January) says one 'would be conducted'.

title: Prayagraj police registered a case over the 25 January 2022 events. The Prayagraj SSP said it was against about 1,000 unidentified people under 13 serious secti
establishes: The count of persons covered is DISPUTED: about 1,000 (PTI/ANI) against 1,500 (Deccan Herald). The sections were not listed in the articles read. The allegation about political funding is the police's, unproven, and denied by no one in the sources read.

title: A local activist who convenes a student platform in Prayagraj told Newslaundry (10 February 2022) that he was named as main accused in the FIR over the protest
establishes: Two sources, but the second does not confirm the arrest, jail term or his role in the FIR, and the spelling of the surname differs between them. The person is not named here. His NHRC remark is his own. No bail order was found. A search for it returned unrelated 2022 matters.

title: No court order, NHRC registration, state human rights commission action or inquiry report concerning the Prayagraj police action of 25 January 2022 was found. T
establishes: Absence in sources searched is not evidence of absence. Routes: NHRC online case search, Allahabad High Court case status, RTI to the Prayagraj Police Commissionerate or SSP office for the suspension orders, the inquiry order and its report, and the FIR; RTI to the UP Home (Police) department.

title: On 17 June 2022 a protest by army recruitment aspirants against the Agnipath scheme at Secunderabad railway station, Telangana, turned violent (a train was set
establishes: Occurrence corroborated by several outlets. The Tribune copy is PTI; the others are separate reports. Cause of death is as reported, from hospital staff quoted by the press; no post-mortem report was read. Who fired is DISPUTED, see HIST-AGN-002. The victim is described in every report as an army job aspirant (some say he had cleared the medical test and was awaiting the written exam). No source read here calls him a student. Interpretation of the scope note: he qualifies as a person who faced violence.

title: Reports conflict on which force fired at Secunderabad. Version A: the Railway Protection Force (RPF) fired, per 'a senior police official' quoted by PTI, per Si
establishes: All officials in these reports are unnamed, except Railway SP B. Anuradha, who is quoted on cases booked only. Reports also differ on ammunition (rubber bullets, aerial firing, bullet injuries reported by the hospital). No source read here gives a ballistic or post-mortem finding. Tribune and Careers360 may share PTI origin. A tweet or statement attributing the firing to state police by a political figure was seen only in a search snippet and is not recorded.

title: Unnamed officials described the decision to fire as collective or as taken on higher instructions. Careers360 quotes an unnamed South Central Railway official s
establishes: These are attributed press accounts from unnamed officials. They place the decision at the level of 'higher' offices in the railway police and/or state police without identifying the office. Do not read the two named officers as having given any order: the source says only that they held talks.

title: The individual or office that gave the order to fire at Secunderabad on 17 June 2022 is not established by any document read for this record. No police statemen
establishes: Searched for statements by the GRP, RPF, Hyderabad police and Telangana DGP, and for a magisterial inquiry, Telangana High Court or NHRC proceeding. Nothing found. A protester quoted by Deccan Chronicle asked 'who gave orders to open fire on us' (reported, unanswered). Absence from search results is not proof no such document exists.

title: Injury and victim details differ across reports. Injured protesters: 12 (Siasat, The Quint), 13 (Careers360, Hans India), 14 (Deccan Chronicle headline; its tex
establishes: Hospital source is Dr Raja Rao, superintendent of Gandhi Hospital, quoted by Deccan Chronicle. No official casualty list was read. Victim: Damera Rakesh of Dabeerpet village, Khanapur mandal, Warangal district, described by The Quint and Tribune as an army aspirant, son of a farmer. Name spelled Damera, Damira and Damodar Rakesh in different reports.

title: The Government Railway Police (GRP), Secunderabad, registered a case against the protesters after the 17 June 2022 violence. SP B. Anuradha is quoted: 'We booke
establishes: FIR number, police station and complainant were not found. This record concerns the case against protesters. No source read reports an FIR or case about the firing or the death.

title: ThePrint reports the railway police case cites Indian Penal Code sections 143, 147, 324, 307, 435, 427, 448, 336, 332 and 341.
establishes: Single source, no FIR copy read. Section list not checked against the FIR.

title: Arrests: Deccan Chronicle (18 June 2022) reports that officials said police detained 26 individuals. The Hans India (25 June 2022) reports 55 persons arrested a
establishes: Police allegation that Subba Rao met job-seekers on 16 and 17 June, urged an attack and supplied masks is the police account as reported by The Hans India; no charge sheet or court finding was read. Revanth Reddy's statement is a political allegation and is attributed to him. The Hans India says police 'will announce his arrest soon', so the arrest was not formally confirmed in that article. Court custody details were not found in a page read.

title: The News Minute (19 June 2022) reports that the Telangana State Human Rights Commission asked the RPF and GRP for a report, with 20 July given as the deadline.
establishes: Single source, and the commission's own order was not found or read. This is the state commission, a body separate from the NHRC. No NHRC action, Telangana High Court petition or magisterial inquiry was found. The report's contents and the commission's outcome are unknown.

title: Telangana Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao announced Rs 25 lakh ex gratia and a government job for a family member of Damera Rakesh on 17 June 2022. A Govern
establishes: The Government Order itself was not read; the account is from press. The Chief Minister is also quoted by Careers360 as blaming the Centre's 'faulty procedures' for the death. That is a political statement with no standing as a finding.

title: Whether any magisterial inquiry, judicial inquiry, NHRC case, Telangana High Court petition, or prosecution or departmental action over the firing exists is not
establishes: Searches for these returned nothing relating to this incident. Treat as a gap to fill by RTI and eCourts search. The gap leaves open whether any exists.

title: On 20 June 2024 Delhi Police detained students outside the Ministry of Education and outside Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's residence in central Delhi,
establishes: All four pages derive from the PTI wire, so this counts as one source family. The count is not established: 'more than two dozen' and 'around 50 / over 50' both appear. Maktoob adds that protesters were pushed into buses after NSUI president Varun Choudhary was dragged away; that is the outlet's account and is attributed to no document. Deccan Herald's version of this story returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The protest is about the UGC-NET cancellation as well as NEET-UG; it is recorded because the same groups were protesting NEET-UG.

title: Force on 20 June 2024: SFI said 'Female students were heckled and manhandled brutally'; DSF said Delhi Police 'attacked and detained several students including
establishes: Both sides are as the PTI-derived reports give them: the organisations allege force, an unnamed police officer denies it. Maktoob carries the allegations and does not carry the denial. The social media video was not seen or located. No injury figures appear in any of the three pages. No finding is made either way.

title: On 24 June 2024 Delhi Police detained 'more than two dozen' students, some of them NSUI members, at Jantar Mantar before a planned march to Parliament, and took
establishes: Both pages are the same PTI report, so this is one source family. Neither alleges excessive force, so this is recorded as detentions with no force alleged. The officer is unnamed and no rank is given. No exact count is given.

title: On the evening of 26 June 2024 Delhi Police detained 'over a dozen' students at Jantar Mantar after a protest by the JNU students' union and other groups. A pol
establishes: Detention only; none of the three pages alleges force on this day. The 'court's order' is not named in any page and was not located. Republic's JNU section carries 'with PTI inputs'; Careers360 names no agency; so independence from the wire is not shown. The Mooknayak (28 June) says the AISA, KYS, Disha and BsCEM strike began on 26 June and the students were 'initially detained' but resumed protesting that evening, via an AISA Delhi University secretary; it does not give a count.

title: On 27 June 2024 Delhi Police used physical force against Indian Youth Congress members protesting over NEET-UG and the Agniveer scheme at Jantar Mantar. The Tri
establishes: Three outlets with their own text (Tribune News Service, Republic Digital Desk, Mooknayak reporter) plus the PTI wire carrying the police account. That the police used force is common ground; whether it was a lathi charge is DISPUTED at HIST-NEET-006. No finding on proportionality or cause.

title: Characterisation of the 27 June 2024 force at Jantar Mantar. Tribune, Republic World and The Mooknayak describe a lathi charge. The Indian Youth Congress 'accus
establishes: Both versions stand. The IYC's slot is given by the PTI report as 10 am to 1 pm, with police saying protesters stayed beyond it; the permission document was not seen. No video was located or viewed. Rank and name of the senior officer are not given.

title: Number detained at Jantar Mantar around 27 and 28 June 2024. ThePrint (PTI, 27 June): 'police said around 60 protesters were detained at the site', in the repor
establishes: The same figure of about 60 is attached to two different groups (IYC protesters in ThePrint, AISA and KYS students in Dinamalar), and the date of the second is not stated. These may be one count described two ways or two counts. They cannot be reconciled from the pages read. The real figure is not established.

title: On 27 June 2024 NSUI members led by president Varun Choudhary entered the National Testing Agency office in Okhla and locked it with a chain and lock. Versions
establishes: No detention or force is reported at the NTA office in the pages read. Medical Dialogues (28 June) covers the entry and an NSUI statement and says nothing about police. Listed because the brief names the NTA office; the documented police action is not at that office.

title: A case was registered against NSUI national president Varun Choudhary over the NTA office incident, under IPC sections 186, 353, 452 and 342/34, according to Di
establishes: Sections are as Dinamalar prints them; they were not checked against an FIR copy. No FIR number, police station, date or copy was found. A separate Careers360 report of 9 July 2024, cited here only in this note, quotes Choudhary saying he was summoned by Delhi Police on 7 July, without naming a case. Whether any case was registered against the IYC is not established.

title: On 2 July 2024 Delhi Police detained 'over a dozen' students who began marching from Patel Chowk metro station towards Parliament after a press conference at th
establishes: Outside June but part of the same 'India against NTA' stir. Detention only; no force alleged in the page. Business Standard's copy returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

title: Who ordered the detentions of 20 June 2024: NOT ESTABLISHED. An unnamed police officer is reported as saying protesters had not obtained permission in the high-
establishes: Level of office: the only actor named in all pages is 'police' (Delhi Police). Delhi Police reports to the Union Home Ministry. No Ministry, Commissioner or station-level statement was found. No individual is named by any document.

title: Prohibitory order on 20 June 2024: Dinamalar says an officer stated the protesters had no permission in a high-security area 'which is under Section 144'; Kashm
establishes: Single wire family. The statement of a police officer is reported; the order is not seen. Who issued it and under which text is UNKNOWN. In force on that date was the CrPC, since BNSS began on 1 July 2024; the section number is repeated only as the source reports it and was not checked against an order.

title: Who gave the order to detain students at Jantar Mantar on 24 June 2024: NOT ESTABLISHED. An officer, unnamed, is reported saying no permission was granted for t
establishes: Only 'police' and an unnamed officer appear. The permission decision itself (who refused, in what document) was not found.

title: Who gave the order to detain students after 5 pm at Jantar Mantar on 26 June 2024, and which court order is meant: NOT ESTABLISHED. The officer cites 'a court's
establishes: The court order was not located and no court is named in the page. No individual is named.

title: Who gave the order for force and detentions against IYC protesters at Jantar Mantar on 27 June 2024: NOT ESTABLISHED. A 'senior police officer', unnamed and unr
establishes: Per ThePrint the IYC had a permitted slot of 10 am to 1 pm; the permission and any later dispersal order were not seen. Documents that could settle this: the permission letter, the order or message directing dispersal, the station diary, the detention memo, and the officer's report of mild force. All would be requested from Delhi Police; the police station with jurisdiction is not identified in any page read.

title: Inquiry, NHRC action, High Court or Supreme Court proceedings about police action against NEET protesters in June 2024: none found.
establishes: Searches returned only proceedings about a different, 2026 protest wave, which are not read or cited here. Nothing was found for June 2024. This is a finding of absence in the pages found only; it leaves open whether any exists.

title: Police action against NEET-UG protesters in Patna or elsewhere in Bihar in June 2024: none found. Search results for Patna lathi charge and tear gas were dated
establishes: Not established either way. The Bihar police items found for 2024 concern the paper-leak investigation, which is not the incident.

title: Injuries to protesters in June 2024 Delhi protests: no figure appears in any page read. The only injury-adjacent claim is the IYC's allegation of beating (HIST-
establishes: No hospital or medical record was found.

title: On Sunday 29 December 2024 aspirants for the 70th BPSC Combined (Preliminary) Competitive Examination, which had been held on 13 December 2024, gathered at Gand
establishes: Four outlets agree on the date, the place, the water cannon and the lathicharge. Scroll's account of the DM's statement comes from PTI; the others report on their own. No primary document (order, report, court record) was read. One source (Drishti IAS, summarising a complaint) dates the lathi charge to 28 December 2024; the four above and the other outlets read say Sunday, which is 29 December 2024. The pages were read through a summarising fetch tool with no files saved, so no sha256 is recorded.

title: Patna's District Magistrate was reported as saying water cannon and 'mild force' were used to disperse protesters who had blocked traffic near JP Golambar. ETV
establishes: Single outlet for the DM's words (ETV Bharat). The quote was checked against the raw page text on 10 October 2026. Protesters and opposition figures describe the force as excessive; those are their unproven allegations.

title: Who gave the order for the water cannon and lathicharge on 29 December 2024 is NOT ESTABLISHED. None of the pages read names the officer or office that ordered
establishes: No order, magistrate's dispersal order, control-room log or deployment order was found online. Records that could be requested: the Patna District Magistrate's order on permission for Gandhi Maidan and any order on dispersal; the Patna SSP's deployment order and magistrate duty list for 29 December 2024; the Gandhi Maidan police station diary for that evening and the FIR; control-room and wireless logs; water cannon and lathi issue records; any report sent to the Home Department or the Chief Secretary. File the same question with the District Magistrate, the SSP Patna, and the Bihar Home Department at the same time.

title: The Patna District Magistrate, Chandrashekhar Singh, told PTI that the administration would not allow students to gather near the Mahatma Gandhi statue at Gandh
establishes: Scroll and Careers360 both attribute the DM's words to PTI, so they share one origin. The administration's account, that protesters went to JP Golambar without permission, blocked the road and argued with magistrates on duty, comes from the administration through Patna Press and is its allegation. Protest-side accounts say the march was peaceful.

title: Whether a prohibitory order (an order restricting assembly under the criminal procedure code in force) was in effect at Gandhi Maidan or JP Golambar on 29 Decem
establishes: Request the District Magistrate's order, if any, together with its date, the section it was issued under and the area it covered. The statutory basis should be filled in by a lawyer against the current text.

title: Injuries and detentions on 29 December 2024. Outlets report that 'several' students were injured and 'some' were detained, with no official count. The Logical I
establishes: The 150 to 200 detention figure appears in one outlet and no other page read gives a count, so it is unconfirmed. No hospital figure or police figure was found. The people affected, as the sources describe them, are aspirants and students of the 70th BPSC preliminary examination; the complaint also refers to women among the protesters. Prashant Kishor of the Jan Suraj Party joined the event; the sources disagree on whether he was at the site when force was used (Patna Press says he left, others do not say).

title: An FIR was registered at Gandhi Maidan police station against 21 named persons, including Jan Suraj Party founder Prashant Kishor and party president Manoj Bhar
establishes: Number of unidentified persons differs: 'nearly 600' (Scroll) and '600 to 700' (Patna Press and ETV Bharat). The DM is reported as the source for the FIR in ETV Bharat and Careers360 coverage. Sections of law, FIR number and date were not stated in any page read. The FIR targets the organisers and is an unproven allegation. Two Patna tutors were also arrested and later granted conditional bail, per Scroll and ETV Bharat.

title: A Bihar-based advocate, unnamed in the page read, filed a complaint with the National Human Rights Commission over the police action against BPSC aspirants in P
establishes: Single source. Drishti IAS dates the police action to 28 December 2024, which conflicts with 29 December in other outlets. No NHRC case number, direction or reply was found. A separate NHRC matter about the District Magistrate slapping an aspirant on 13 December 2024 was seen only in search results and was not fetched, so it is not recorded here. The NHRC clippings PDF returned HTTP 404 and was not read.

title: Independent MP Pappu Yadav is reported as saying that Bihar's Governor spoke to the BPSC chairman and said he would ask the District Magistrate and the Superint
establishes: Single source, second-hand. Scroll gives no direct Governor quote. No answer from the DM or SP was found.

title: The Patna High Court (Acting Chief Justice Ashutosh Kumar and Justice Partha Sarathy) dismissed petitions seeking cancellation of the 70th BPSC preliminary exam
establishes: Case title given by LiveLaw: Anand Legal Aid Forum Trust vs Bihar Public Service Commission and Ors. The judgment itself was not read. No court proceeding specifically about the lathicharge was found; lawyers' offers of free legal aid to protesters were seen only in search results. Court records worth requesting: the writ petitions, any counter-affidavit by the State or the District Magistrate that describes the 29 December events, and the certified judgment.

title: No magisterial inquiry, departmental inquiry or judicial inquiry into the 29 December 2024 police action, and no outcome of any such inquiry, was found.
establishes: Absence from searches is not evidence that none exists. Ask the Bihar Home Department and the Patna District Magistrate whether any inquiry was ordered, by whom, and its report.

title: In Patna in early May 2026, aspirants demanding the fourth phase of the BPSC Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE-4) notification marched from the Patna Science
establishes: Two outlets agree on the event, the place and the use of lathicharge. They differ on the day (see HIST-BPSCB-002) and on the starting point (Science College per ETV Bharat, Patna College per National Herald). No primary document was read.

title: The date of the TRE-4 march and police action is DISPUTED. ETV Bharat (published 8 May 2026) says the clash happened on Thursday, which is 7 May 2026, though a
establishes: Neither outlet gives a calendar date in the text read; the day of week is the only dating. Resolve with the FIR date or a police station diary entry.

title: Patna City SP (Central), identified as Diksha in National Herald's report, said some protesters became aggressive and tried to break barricades and: 'During the
establishes: The SP quote is from one outlet. ETV Bharat reports 'several candidates were reportedly injured' with no count. No injury count from either side, and no hospital record, was found. The victims, as sources describe them, are teaching-job aspirants (TRE-4 candidates); the protest leader named in both outlets is Dilip Kumar.

title: An FIR was registered at Gandhi Maidan police station on a magistrate's complaint against about 5,000 unidentified TRE-4 aspirants for disrupting traffic, breac
establishes: Allegations in an FIR are not findings. Sections of law, FIR number and date were not stated. 'Detained' versus 'arrested' differs between the outlets. That the complaint came from a magistrate indicates a magistrate was present, but no page says a magistrate ordered force.

title: Who gave the order for the lathicharge on the TRE-4 protesters in May 2026 is NOT ESTABLISHED. Neither page names the officer or office that ordered force, and
establishes: Records to request: the magistrate's complaint that started the FIR, magistrate and police deployment orders for the day, Gandhi Maidan police station diary, control-room logs, and any dispersal order. Ask the District Magistrate Patna, SSP Patna and the Bihar Home Department.

title: Whether a prohibitory order was in force, whether any inquiry was ordered, and whether the Patna High Court or the NHRC has acted on the May 2026 TRE-4 police a
establishes: Searches were limited to news coverage. eCourts, NHRC case status and the Bihar Assembly question lists were not searched.

title: On 20 September 2018 a protest by students and parents against the posting of Urdu and Sanskrit teachers at Darivit High School, Islampur block, Uttar Dinajpur
establishes: The two deaths are named in the judgment (paras 4, 12), which is the document this archive relies on for the names. Ages differ: Indian Express and Hindustan Times (2018) give 19 and 21 for the two. The judgment calls the dead 'boys' and 'students' in the NHRC extract and does not give ages. Whether either was a minor is not established here. Both are described by the press as former students of the school. Indian Express (20 September 2018) first reported one death; the second death was reported the next day (HT, 23 September 2018: one died 'on the spot', the other 'on Friday').

title: Police used tear gas and rubber bullets at Darivit High School on 20 September 2018. This is stated by the police themselves: the High Court records the gist of
establishes: The SP's quotation is from The Indian Express, 20 September 2018, and is a newspaper's report of a spoken statement. The FIR account is a primary document as recited by the court (the FIR itself was not read). The same sources attribute the first use of force to a mob attacking the police. That attribution is the police version and is not found by the court.

title: Whether police use of force on 20 September 2018 was excessive, and what it included, is DISPUTED. (a) Police and State version: police were 'suddenly attacked
establishes: No finding of guilt or intent is made here. The NHRC report itself was not read; only the extracts quoted in the judgment. The judgment says the NHRC report 'may be without jurisdiction and cannot technically or legally be called a statutory report' (para 47) because the State Human Rights Commission had taken cognisance first, and the State asked the court to ignore it entirely (para 29).

title: Who fired the bullets that killed two men is DISPUTED. (a) Police and State: police deny firing bullets (SP quoted in Indian Express, 20 September 2018, and Hin
establishes: The court's statements are made in deciding to transfer the investigation and are described by the court as reasons to doubt the CID's work, not as a trial finding on who fired. Nobody has been convicted or charged on the court's reading in the documents read. The weapon, and who held it, are not established in any document read.

title: Who gave the order for police to go to Darivit High School, to enter or break through to the school gate, and to use lathis, tear gas and rubber bullets: NOT ES
establishes: Level of office: the only rank the judgment places at the scene is the Inspector-in-Charge of the police station, as the FIR's own account. Whether the Sub-Divisional Police Officer, the Superintendent of Police or the District Magistrate was present or gave any direction is not stated in any document read. The Indian Express (20 September 2018) quotes the District Magistrate as saying he was 'waiting for the police report' and the SP as saying police 'have fired rubber bullets and tear gas shells', and says nothing about who ordered either. Documents that could settle it are listed at HIST-DAR-014 and HIST-DAR-015.

title: Who gave the order to fire live ammunition, if police did so: NOT ESTABLISHED. Police deny that any live firing by police took place. The High Court says in a p
establishes: Quoted because it is the one passage in a primary document that raises the question of an order to fire. It names no officer, office or political figure as having given one. Para 19(h) records the petitioners' submission that only the CBI 'can investigate the role of influential political persons in the incident and the role of the State police in the death of the two boys'; that is the petitioners' submission.

title: On 23 September 2018 the father of one of the dead men made a complaint that named four people as responsible for the incident: Sumit Kumar, Superintendent of P
establishes: The complaint names these people as responsible for the incident. The judgment does not say the complaint alleges any of them gave an order, and the court makes no finding against any of them. Names appear here only because the judgment records them and this record quotes it. The complaint also appears in the judgment as dated both 23 September 2018 (paras 7, 62) and 25 September 2018 (para 19(a)); the two dates are the court's own inconsistency. A separate complaint by the father of the other dead man, dated 21 September 2018, is recorded at para 8.

title: FIR No. 611 of 2018 was registered on 20 September 2018 at Islampur police station by the police themselves (suo motu; the judgment says 'The original FIR was r
establishes: Internal inconsistencies in the court's text: the charge sheet is 'no. 860 of 2022 dated 7th November, 2022' at para 5 and 'no. 879 of 2022 dated 25.11.2022' at para 73, which is held in abeyance. LiveLaw gives 7 November 2022. The NHRC extract gives the transfer to CB-CID as 27 September 2018 (para 25, vii), against 25 September 2018 in the court's own recital. The NHRC extract lists section 332 as well. No police officer is recorded in the judgment as named in the FIR as an accused. The FIR itself was not read. Number of arrests on 20 September 2018 is not stated; the NHRC extract says police arrested 'some named accused in the night of 20.09.2018'.

title: No FIR or case was registered on the separate assault at Golapara village, in which the families say the two injured men were waylaid and beaten while being tak
establishes: VERIFIED applies only to the court's record that no separate FIR was registered. The cause and place of each death are DISPUTED between the court's own paragraphs and the press. Indian Express (20 September 2018) said one man was 'declared brought dead at Islampur sub-divisional hospital'. NDTV (23 September 2018) said the second man died of gunshot wounds at North Bengal Medical College. A second post-mortem was requested and, per the judgment, never conducted (para 19(f)).

title: Injury counts conflict. CID report as recorded by the court: 12 police personnel and 3 civilians injured (para 10). FIR gist: three civilians and one police off
establishes: No count of injured students, or of injuries to police from the other side's account, is verified. The CID figure for police injuries comes from a document the court read but this archive has not. Of the civilians with bullet injuries, one survived with a thigh wound according to the NHRC extract (para 25, iii); this archive does not name him because the sources do not establish his age.

title: Inquiries into police conduct. (1) State Human Rights Commission: took cognisance on 25 September 2018 after a report in a local Bengali newspaper and has since
establishes: The NHRC report itself and its case number were not read or found; only the conclusions quoted at para 25. The NHRC conclusions include findings on the school's teacher-posting decisions (a decision on 18 September 2018 to withdraw the posting, reversed on 20 September 2018 by the district education department) that bear on cause only. No departmental, magisterial or judicial inquiry by the State into the police conduct is recorded in the judgment. The NHRC extract says senior officers could have ordered 'an impartial enquiry by a senior officer of another range or a magistrate' and did not (para 25, viii).

title: Calcutta High Court, single judge Rajasekhar Mantha, judgment of 10 May 2023 (hearing concluded 1 May 2023) in three writ petitions filed on 4 October 2018 (WPA
establishes: Two other petition sets (the SHRC's and the NHRC's positions) are summarised at paras 21 to 24 and 43 to 44. The judgment does not name the police officer who led the force. The ruling was reported by LiveLaw (11 May 2023), LawBeat (11 May 2023) and PTI (10 May 2023). The copy read is hosted by Verdictum; the court's own copy was not fetched, and the judgment says parties are to act on the court website's copy (para 80).

title: Appeal and aftermath. REPORTED (Law Trend, 3 April 2024): a Division Bench headed by Chief Justice T.S. Sivagnanam left the single-bench order in force, agreed
establishes: The Division Bench orders themselves were not found or read. The 2024 item rests on one outlet. The statement that compensation was not paid is the families' counsel's, as reported, and is not established. Millennium Post and the Times of India report the same hearing, so they may share a source in court; they are separate publications and are treated here as two reports that leave the facts unproven. Search found no report of an NIA charge sheet, arrest, or any action against a police officer.

title: Records that could be requested to answer who gave the order, drawn from the documents the NHRC team says it asked for in October 2018 and did not receive (judg
establishes: These are the NHRC's own request list and show which records the NHRC considered relevant. This archive has not seen any of them. Holder: Islampur police station and Uttar Dinajpur police for the logs and registers; the District Magistrate for orders; the CID (case diary now with the NIA) for the investigation file. RTI replies on records held by the NIA or on a pending investigation may be refused; a lawyer should say which exemptions apply. The case diary and charge sheet are also before the court and can be applied for as certified copies. The deployment chart and arms register are the records most likely to show which rank signed off on the deployment and on issue of rifles.

title: Other records that could be requested: (a) the State's affidavit in opposition and the CID report filed in WPA 20733 of 2018 and connected petitions, and the NH
establishes: The CID report and the affidavits would be the first place the State has said, on affidavit, what was authorised and by whom; the judgment's summary of them does not say. None of these was read. The NHRC case number is not given in the judgment.

title: Level of office at which the decisions to deploy, use force and fire were taken, summary: ESTABLISHED that the force at the school was the West Bengal Police fr
establishes: Four people are named as 'responsible for the incident' in a complaint recorded at para 7 (HIST-DAR-007); the court makes no finding against them and the complaint is not recorded as alleging an order. The investigating agency that held the case for four years was the State CID, a part of the same State police; the court says its investigation was perfunctory and that it may have been inhibited from examining a police or political role (para 71). The NIA now holds the case; its findings are not public.

title: On 2 May 2018 a group of Hindu right-wing activists came to the Aligarh Muslim University campus over the portrait of Muhammad Ali Jinnah in the students' union
establishes: The occurrence on 2 May is agreed. The group's size and organisation are DISPUTED between outlets and no source read here is a primary document. Arms: Tribune says pistols and revolvers, VICE says witnesses described hockey sticks and guns; these are unproven student and witness accounts as reported. The Newsclick article quotes the Additional District Magistrate as saying the probe found no plan to attack Mr Ansari; AMU students' union and teachers' association said the opposite (see Quint 3 May). No finding on intent is made here.

title: How the activists left police custody on 2 May 2018 is DISPUTED. (a) AMU's proctor, per PTI: security staff overpowered a small group around 2 p.m. and handed t
establishes: Version (c) is from an official who conducted the probe but is reported in a single interview; the report was not read. Version (a) is the university's account relayed by PTI. No document read records who at the police station decided to let them go, or on whose instruction. Level of office: unknown. The Newsclick article places the failure with 'the then Station House Officer of Civil Lines police station' regarding the earlier entry onto campus only. The article does not say the SHO ordered the release.

title: Police used a lathi charge and tear gas on AMU students on 2 May 2018 after the students demanded action against the activists. Reports differ on which was used
establishes: Use of force is agreed across independent outlets; the weapon mix is not. The police version is thin: no police statement on why force was used appears in the pages read. Newslaundry says unidentified men pelted stones during the lathi charge and that there was no police firing. The Week (4 May) states without attribution that students 'pelted stones at journalists'; this is the outlet's own sentence and no police source is given. Allegations of excess are the students' and teachers' (AMUSU, AMUTA); no court or inquiry finding on proportionality was found.

title: Where the students were heading when they were stopped is reported as the Dodhpur police station by VICE. Other outlets read say only that students were marchin
establishes: The archive's premise that students marched to Dodhpur is supported by one fetched source only. A search summary claimed Hindustan Times names Civil Lines for the march; the Hindustan Times page could only be read as far as the opening lines, which say 'a police complaint' with no station, so that was not relied on. Marked REPORTED. Time of the march: around 4 p.m. per VICE alone.

title: Injury figures for 2 May 2018 are DISPUTED: at least three students (Deccan Chronicle, 2 May); at least six people, with hospital sources saying about 20 studen
establishes: All figures are press figures; no hospital record or police return was read. The 13 police injured appears only via ANI. The numbers may be counting different times or different groups. Names of injured students are deliberately not recorded here. Medical records are the way to settle this (see notes file).

title: The news reports read record no detention or arrest of students by police on 2 May 2018. Police later arrested two people from the activists' side (reported 6 M
establishes: No FIR copy, FIR number, police station or section was seen. A search snippet mentioned Sections 147 and 153A for the two arrested; the pages fetched did not confirm sections, so none are recorded. 'No detention of students found' is an absence in the pages read only; it leaves open whether any happened. The Wire LiveWire (8 May) also reports the union demanding that the FIR against AMU students be revoked, which is the same claim from the same side. Whether an FIR was registered against the activists is not shown by any page read: students say police refused (Tribune, Newslaundry); the later arrests suggest some case existed but the case is not identified.

title: A magisterial inquiry into the 2 May 2018 violence was ordered by the District Magistrate, Aligarh, on Friday 4 May 2018 (Hindustan Times, 5 May, headline 'Magi
establishes: The order itself (number, date, terms of reference, named officer) was not found or read. Date of order as 4 May comes from the Hindustan Times headline and opening line only; VICE says the Chief Minister promised an inquiry by 4 May, which is a different thing. The Week (4 May) gives no deadline; no source read states a deadline. Office: District Magistrate, Aligarh. Whether the 'magisterial inquiry' is the same as the 'probe' in item 8 rests on an assumption made by the sources.

title: Outcome of the magisterial probe: the Additional District Magistrate (Finance) who conducted it told Newsclick in January 2019 that his report, submitted to the
establishes: Single source, and it relays the officer's own account of his report. The report was not read. Students' union leader Mashkoor Usmani is quoted calling it 'a mere formality' and asking 'Who is responsible for that lathi-charge?'; a student is quoted asking 'on whose orders' students were attacked, which the report as described does not answer. Mid-probe, on 9 May 2018, the District Magistrate said the probe 'has identified all those who indulged in hooliganism and violence' (PTI via india.com). No action taken on the SHO was found.

title: WHO GAVE THE ORDER for the lathi charge and tear gas on students on 2 May 2018: NOT ESTABLISHED. No FIR, order, affidavit, judgment or inquiry report was found
establishes: Sources read for this finding, listed here because none contains the answer: VICE (vice.com article above), Deccan Chronicle (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/020518/protests-clashes-aligarh-muslim-university-muhammad-ali-jinnah-photo.html), Tribune (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/amu-jinnah-row-turns-violent-583533), The Week/PTI, The Quint, Newslaundry, SabrangIndia, The Wire LiveWire, Newsclick, National Herald. Level of office: the only institutions named in the force are the UP Police generally and the Rapid Action Force (two RAF companies, per the District Magistrate to Deccan Chronicle). Officials who appear in the coverage and who must NOT be assumed to have given any order: the District Magistrate (CB Singh in Deccan Chronicle; Chandra Bhushan Singh in SabrangIndia), the Senior Superintendent of Police (Ajay Kumar Sahni, quoted by PTI on 9 May on the political angle and Section 144), and a City Superintendent of Police (Atul Srivastava, quoted by PTI only on tightened security). National Herald (6 May) reports that an Additional Superintendent of Police was transferred and that students criticised his role as 'shameful'; no document ties him to any order. Section 144 was imposed and internet suspended on 4 May (after the force), which is a separate order. Documents that could settle it: see amu2018-notes.md.

title: WHO GAVE THE ORDER to release the activists from police custody on 2 May 2018: NOT ESTABLISHED, and the fact of a police release is itself DISPUTED (item 2). No
establishes: Level of office: the station level (Civil Lines police station) is the only location any source gives, and the proctor's contrary account says a larger group took them away. Nothing read says the Station House Officer, a senior officer or the district administration decided anything about the release. The station's General Diary entry for 2 May 2018 would record the handover and the departure; see notes file.

title: AMU Students' Union said it would petition the Allahabad High Court against the district administration and police for inaction (The Quint, 3 May 2018, citing t
establishes: These are statements of intent and demands. No petition, case number, notice or order was found, and no judicial probe was found to have been ordered. The Quint, The Week and Two Circles each report the intention separately, but the court filing itself is not shown, so the filing is not recorded as a fact here.

title: Whether any court petition, High Court or Supreme Court proceeding, judicial inquiry, National Human Rights Commission complaint, disciplinary action against po
establishes: Searches for Allahabad High Court, Supreme Court and NHRC proceedings on these events returned nothing relevant. An Allahabad High Court report on an AMU student's challenge to a different FIR over a students' union election matter appeared in results and is not about this incident. Absence from a web search is not proof none exists; High Court case status and the NHRC case search need to be checked directly.

title: On Friday 23 March 2018 a march of students and teachers from Jawaharlal Nehru University towards Parliament, called by the JNU Students' Union and the JNU Teac
establishes: Five separate newspaper reports agree on the stop, the water cannons and the broad reasons for the march. Place names differ between reports: near INA Market (The Hindu, Hindustan Times, Scroll.in), near Sanjay Jheel or Laxmi Bai Nagar (Indian Express, Times of India), and before the Safdarjung flyover (Sabrang India, National Herald). The reports read are all secondary; no police order, permission letter or court record was read. Use of lathis is disputed, see HIST-JNU18-005.

title: Size of the march: the Indian Express, NewsClick and the New Indian Express put it at more than 1,000 students and teachers; Sabrang India says 'thousands'; the
establishes: The figure of about 500 supplied in the research brief was not found in any source read, and the sources read give a higher number. These are reporters' and officials' estimates, with no count from a record behind them. Treat the 500 figure as UNVERIFIED unless a source for it is found.

title: Who gave the order to stop the march near INA Market: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document read for this record names a person or an office that ordered the stop. The o
establishes: Level of office: the institution all sources name is the Delhi Police, which sabrangindia.in describes as under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The rank at which the decision was taken (station, district, range, headquarters or the Union Home Ministry) is unknown. The anonymous 'orders to stop us' remark is a student's recollection of what a policeman said, reported by National Herald; no senior officer is named as the source of any order. The spokespersons named in the reports (the Special Commissioner of Police who is the chief spokesperson, and the DCP who is the public relations officer) spoke to the press after the event; no document read says either gave any order on 23 March 2018 and this archive makes no such claim. See HIST-JNU18-004 for the permission conflict and HIST-JNU18-017 to 021 for records that could settle the question.

title: Permission for the march is DISPUTED. Version A (Delhi Police chief spokesperson, The Hindu): 'Permission for the protest march was denied but the students star
establishes: Versions A and B are both attributed to the same Delhi Police spokesperson in different newspapers and do not obviously fit together: refusing permission and agreeing a symbolic march are different positions. No permission request, reply or minute of the meetings was read. The Hindu also quotes a student saying the police 'had been informed about the march beforehand', which is not the same as permission. The archive does not choose between the versions.

title: Use of lathis or batons is DISPUTED. Students and their union say police baton-charged the marchers (Scroll.in: 'baton charged the protestors, injuring many, th
establishes: The wording of the Indian Express report on the chief spokesperson is ambiguous about whether he accepted a lathi charge happened or was answering the allegation. No video or police record was read. Use of water cannons is not disputed: police tweets quoted by Newslaundry and the chief spokesperson (The Hindu: 'Finally, water cannons were used to control the crowd') both confirm it.

title: Account of what provoked the force is DISPUTED. Delhi Police version: students 'turned violent, broke barricades and assaulted policemen' (chief spokesperson, T
establishes: Both sides filed or announced complaints; see HIST-JNU18-013 and HIST-JNU18-012. Shopkeepers on the route told National Herald the march did not disturb traffic, while Hindustan Times reports traffic jams in south Delhi and diversions on Sansad Marg ordered by Traffic Police. No finding of any court on who was the aggressor was found.

title: Injury counts. Police claim: 41 police personnel were injured, including the station house officers of Hauz Khas and Safdarjung Enclave (chief spokesperson, The
establishes: The 41 figure comes from police and appears in two newspapers that both cite police, so it counts as one source. No medical record, AIIMS record or police injury list was read. Whether any person was hospitalised is not stated in the reports read.

title: Detention counts are DISPUTED. The Hindu (citing police): 23 students detained around 6.30 p.m., released later, protesters dispersed around 9.30 p.m. Hindustan
establishes: The range is 20 to 23 and the differences may be rounding. The release time differs: Hindu says dispersal about 9.30 p.m. per police; CJP (secondary, quoting a CPI(M) leader's account) says students were allowed to leave only after 11 p.m. The place of detention is given as Defence Colony police station by the Indian Express; the CJP account says students were taken to a 'licensing section'. No detention memo or station diary was read.

title: Allegations that women students were manhandled. National Herald reports JNU students saying 'several girl students were molested by policemen', that a woman st
establishes: Allegations are attributed to the students and the union; no finding of fact exists in the sources read. No student is named here. The CJP account is second-hand (a politician's description of what she saw at a police station). The police statements read concern journalists only (HIST-JNU18-010). The brief's description 'allegations of women manhandled' is accurate as an allegation.

title: Allegations by journalists. Several journalists said they were manhandled or molested by police at the march: a reporter of the Indian Express alleged an office
establishes: The existence of the complaints and the police apology are corroborated across independent outlets. The allegations themselves remain allegations. The journalists are not named here. The India.com article titled 'Police apologises, assures inquiry in journalist molestation case' returned HTTP 403 to the fetch and was not read, so it is not cited.

title: Internal police action after the march: Delhi Police ordered a vigilance inquiry into the complaint against the SHO of Delhi Cantt police station; the SHO was s
establishes: All four reports trace to the Delhi Police public relations officer or to officials speaking to the press, so the underlying origin is police statements, reported by independent outlets. No order of suspension or transfer was read. The police statements describe disciplinary steps against rank-and-file and an SHO; none describes any inquiry into the decision to stop the march or to use water cannons or lathis.

title: On Monday 26 March 2018 Delhi Police registered an FIR at Sarojini Nagar police station on the journalist's complaint against the SHO of Delhi Cantt police stat
establishes: The section number conflicts inside The Hindu report (354A in the narration, 354 in the PRO quote). The FIR number, date of registration beyond 'Monday', and the copy of the FIR were not found. The outcome of the Crime Branch investigation (chargesheet, closure report, trial, departmental result) was searched for and not found: UNKNOWN. The officer is unnamed in this record because the sources read are news reports of an allegation.

title: Delhi Police registered an FIR against JNU students over the march at Sarojini Nagar police station: at least 22 identified students and several unidentified (S
establishes: The existence of the FIR is corroborated by two outlets; the section list is from NewsClick alone and is unconfirmed. FIR number, date and text not found. Whether a chargesheet was filed, or the case withdrawn, quashed or closed, was searched for and not found: UNKNOWN. The Delhi Police had not, as of NewsClick's report of 26 March 2018, registered any FIR on the students' allegations of assault by police.

title: The JNU Students' Union filed a complaint at Sarojini Nagar police station on Monday 26 March 2018 against Delhi Police for 'brutally assaulting students and mo
establishes: Outcome UNKNOWN. A copy of the complaint and any receipt or diary entry could be requested; see HIST-JNU18-019.

title: The National Commission for Women ordered a probe. The NCW Acting Chairperson Rekha Sharma said: 'We have ordered a probe and sent a team today to meet the poli
establishes: The Indian Express and Hindustan Times reports are the same PTI wire and count as one source; Newslaundry is the second. The NCW team's findings, any report to the Delhi Police Commissioner and any follow-up were searched for and not found: UNKNOWN. The NCW's own press release for 24 March 2018 was not located.

title: Journalists' bodies petitioned the Union Home Minister's office. The Times of India reports a group of journalists went to the Union home minister's office on M
establishes: A memorandum to the Home Minister's office would be a record held by the Ministry of Home Affairs. Any reply is UNKNOWN.

title: Who gave the order for water cannons and for the lathi charge (or whatever force was used): NOT ESTABLISHED. The Delhi Police posts quoted by Newslaundry say po
establishes: Level of office unknown. The Hindustan Times reports the SHOs of Hauz Khas and Safdarjung Enclave were among the injured police and Scroll.in reports the Delhi Cantt SHO was deployed on special duty in the INA Market area, which tells who was at the scene and says nothing about who commanded it. Documents that could settle it: HIST-JNU18-019 to HIST-JNU18-021.

title: Whether any prohibitory order (a section 144 order of the former Code of Criminal Procedure) was in force on 23 March 2018 along the route or around Parliament:
establishes: Nothing in the pages read says an order existed or did not exist. The Delhi Police spokesperson's statement was that permission was denied, which is a different thing from a prohibitory order. A request for any order issued by the Delhi Police for 22 and 23 March 2018 would settle it; see HIST-JNU18-019.

title: Records that could be requested to answer who gave the order. From Delhi Police, through the Union RTI route for Delhi described in this archive: the JNU Studen
establishes: Which Delhi Police district office received the march application is not stated in any source read; the PIO must be found from the Delhi Police RTI directory. Detention memos and diary entries are the likely places a named officer would appear. No statement is made about whether these records still exist. All routes named are lawful requests.

title: Records that could be requested on the injuries and the inquiries: the vigilance inquiry report on the complaint against the SHO (Delhi Police); the Crime Branc
establishes: The vigilance report is internal and may be refused under the exemptions for investigations or personal information; a refusal would itself be a record. Medical records are personal information and can be sought by the patient, or by the court. The NCW is the body the Indian Express and Hindustan Times name as ordering the probe.

title: Records that could be requested from the courts and the Ministry: certified copies of the FIR registered against the students and the FIR registered against the
establishes: The statement before a magistrate is a court record and falls outside RTI records. Whether the Delhi Police publish FIRs online for 2018 was not checked here. The case numbers, court names and dates other than 26 March 2018 are not known.

title: Level of office at which each decision was taken, summary. ESTABLISHED to the standard of news reports: the actor is the Delhi Police (CORROBORATED, HIST-JNU18-
establishes: No primary document (order, FIR, diary, court record, Commission report) was read for any item, so nothing in this file reaches VERIFIED. Every source is a news report or an advocacy site, and all police statements are as reported. No outcome was found for the Crime Branch case, the FIR against students, the JNU Students' Union complaint or the NCW probe.

title: On 18 November 2019, the first day of the Winter Session of Parliament, students of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) marched from the campus towards Parliament
establishes: Occurrence of the stop and of detentions agrees across five outlets. The count is treated separately (HIST-JNUF-002). Police stations named differ between outlets (the reporter's diary adds Vasant Vihar and RK Puram). No primary document was found for this day.

title: Number detained on 18 November 2019 differs between reports. Newslaundry and Onmanorama say about 100. The Indian Express reports a Delhi Police Additional PRO
establishes: Both versions are kept. The 50 figure appears in early same-day reporting and the 100 figure in later reporting, including one attributed to the police themselves, so the gap may be timing, but no document reconciles them. The names of the police spokespersons are in the Indian Express article and are not repeated here because no primary document names them.

title: Whether police used lathis on 18 November 2019 is disputed. Newslaundry, The Wire LiveWire, Scroll.in, the Deccan Herald and The Indian Express report a lathich
establishes: Quotes marked from The Indian Express were read in full text. Quotes from Newslaundry, Onmanorama, The Wire and Scroll.in were returned by a summarising fetch tool and should be rechecked against the pages before publication. The police statement itself (a press note) was not found.

title: Injury figures for 18 November 2019 conflict. Police, per PTI text in The Tribune: 'nearly 30 police personnel and 15 students were injured during the eight-hou
establishes: No medico-legal or hospital record was read. Individuals are not named here; the names are in the cited articles.

title: Reports say Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (a prohibition on assembly of four or more people) was in force around the Parliament area on 18 Novem
establishes: Corroboration is of outlets reporting that the prohibition applied. The order itself was not found or read, so its date, text, area and issuer are all unconfirmed. The outlets share a common source in what police told reporters, so this is weaker than five independent sightings of the order. The phrase 'general orders' is the police's own and does not identify an instrument.

title: Who imposed or issued the Section 144 prohibition, or other prohibitory 'general orders', applying to the 18 November 2019 march: NOT ESTABLISHED. Scroll.in att
establishes: Announcing an order at the scene is not the same as issuing it. The level of office that issued it (police headquarters, district, or other) is unknown. See HIST-JNUF-024 for where the text could be requested.

title: Who ordered the detentions on 18 November 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. A Delhi Police Additional PRO is quoted by The Indian Express as saying 100 students were detai
establishes: Level of office: the only actor the sources attribute detentions to is Delhi Police. The rank is unknown.

title: Who ordered any use of force (lathi blows, pushing back, water cannon) on 18 November 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. Delhi Police deny that lathicharge or force was use
establishes: No document read names any officer or office as ordering force. Because the police version is that no force was used, a document naming an order would itself contradict the police account, which is a reason to request deployment and duty records (HIST-JNUF-024).

title: Level of police presence on 18 November 2019, per police statements reported by The Indian Express: 'At least 15 senior police officers were present at the prot
establishes: This establishes who was present according to the police. Single-origin claim (police statement relayed by two outlets). No deployment order was found.

title: Students and the Newslaundry reporter's diary allege that streetlights were switched off near Safdarjung during the evening of 18 November 2019 as police began
establishes: An allegation by protesters and one reporter. No document or independent record found. Who, if anyone, switched the lights off is unknown.

title: Delhi Police registered two FIRs over the 18 November 2019 protest, on 19 November 2019: one at Kishangarh police station and one at Lodhi Colony police station
establishes: The existence of two FIRs is reported by three outlets. The section split differs: The Tribune gives sections only for Lodhi Colony, Careers360 gives 186 and 353 for Kishangarh. No FIR number, text or list of accused was read, and no page names an accused. JNU students' union demanded withdrawal of any FIR against students. Status of both FIRs is unknown (HIST-JNUF-022).

title: On 19 November 2019 opposition members raised the police action against JNU students in Parliament. The Deccan Herald reports that Rajya Sabha proceedings were
establishes: A Zero Hour mention is not a written answer. A search for a Home Ministry written answer on the 18 November march in the 2019 Winter Session returned none; the sansad.in question archive was not itself searched, so absence is not established. Lead for a legislature route: ask a member to table a question to the Ministry of Home Affairs on who authorised the deployment and Section 144.

title: Delhi Police inquiry into the lathicharge allegations of 18 November 2019: the Newslaundry reporter's diary quotes a post by the Delhi Police PRO, via ANI, sayi
establishes: The social media post was not itself retrieved. Outcome unknown. This is a single secondary relay of a police statement.

title: On 9 December 2019 JNU students marched from the campus towards Rashtrapati Bhavan to petition the President over the hostel fee hike. Reports that police lathi
establishes: The police denial rests on one outlet and was not found in a police statement. The Newslaundry piece quotes an unnamed police official: 'These are kids. We don't want to beat them up but we are left with no choice.' A DCP is quoted there as saying students 'are being dropped back at the campus'. The Hindu says the march left campus at 2 pm escorted by police and paramilitary personnel.

title: Detentions on 9 December 2019: the students' union president said 'Several students, including women, have been detained by police' (The Tribune). The Hindu rep
establishes: Whether the removals were legal detentions or transport back to campus is characterised differently by the students and the police. No detention number or station was found.

title: Injuries on 9 December 2019: The Tribune quotes a protester saying 'Over 30 students were injured'; The Hindu says 'Several students were injured'; Newslaundry
establishes: The over-30 figure is a single protester's claim. Treat as unverified as a number.

title: Who gave the order for the lathicharges, the detentions or the stopping of the 9 December 2019 march: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Hindu names no officer. Newslaundry q
establishes: Level of office: the sources attribute the actions to Delhi Police and, for escort and barricades, to police and paramilitary personnel. The Hindu says the march was escorted by police and paramilitary personnel. Rank of the decision maker unknown. The DCP's name appears in Newslaundry and is not repeated because no primary document names that officer or ties them to an order.

title: Whether any prohibitory order (Section 144 or equivalent) was in force for the 9 December 2019 march: no page read states one. The Hindu, The Tribune, NewsMobil
establishes: Absence from five news reports does not show no order existed. Request the order for that date from the issuing authority if any.

title: Whether an FIR was registered over the 9 December 2019 march: none was found in any page read or search result.
establishes: Search of news coverage only; Delhi Police FIR portal not searched.

title: The place of the first 9 December 2019 lathicharge differs between reports. Newslaundry says it was as students came out under the flyover near Bhikaji Cama Pla
establishes: These are neighbouring parts of the same stretch of road and may describe the same events from different vantage points. Kept as a conflict because no source reconciles them.

title: Delhi High Court, single judge (Justice Rajiv Shakdher), 24 January 2020, on a petition by the JNU Students' Union through its president and office bearers chal
establishes: This is the fee dispute that the marches concerned and says nothing on police conduct. Case number and the order text were not retrieved. Outcome after 28 February 2020 not checked. The retrieved page gives the case details as summarised by the reporter.

title: Court proceedings about police conduct on 18 November or 9 December 2019, and the outcome of the FIRs of 19 November 2019 (charge sheet, closure, withdrawal, di
establishes: Not searched on eCourts or Indian Kanoon. Outcome of the FIRs is unknown. A petition to the Delhi High Court on the 15 December 2019 Jamia events was decided on 5 October 2026 (see HIST-JMI-016) and is a separate matter.

title: Who could be asked for the order and the records: the pages read show Delhi Police as the acting force, with the Ministry of Home Affairs as the ministry Parlia
establishes: Placeholder for the chain-of-authority question. Per SOURCING.md, Delhi Police reports to the Ministry of Home Affairs, so the Union RTI route applies.

title: Records that could be requested to settle who gave the order, for both dates: (1) copies of the two FIRs registered at Kishangarh and Lodhi Colony police statio
establishes: These are records only; nothing here is claimed to exist. FIRs are generally public documents. Expect refusals on investigation-related material and plan an appeal. Retention periods may have run since 2019, and a destruction answer is itself evidence.

title: Summary of the order question for the JNU fee-hike marches of 18 November and 9 December 2019: ESTABLISHED, per reporting, that Delhi Police (with paramilitary
establishes: Summary record. The highest rank the sources place at the scene on 18 November is 'Special CP', per the police statement relayed by The Indian Express; presence is not an order. On 9 December the highest designation in the pages read is a DCP.

title: Students from Cotton University and other Guwahati colleges marched towards the state secretariat at Dispur on 11 December 2019 and police used lathis and tear
establishes: Three independent news accounts, one of them a participant's. No primary document (police report, FIR, court record) read. Exact locations, times and number of lathicharge or tear gas rounds are not given. Do not conflate with the firing deaths of 11 and 12 December, which are a separate matter (HIST-COT-012). The Tribune (PTI) the same day also reports police using tear gas and batons on protesters in Guwahati, 'a majority of them students', but does not name the Dispur march.

title: Injuries at the 11 December 2019 Dispur march: Deccan Herald reports 'at least two TV journalists were hurt in the police lathi-charge'. A later complaint by th
establishes: The Students' Forum account is an allegation by the complainant, reported by The Sentinel on 20 December 2019; it is not dated to the 11 December march specifically in the article and may cover the agitation generally. Student leaders told PTI (via The Tribune) that 'many agitators were injured' on 11 December, without a count. Hospital records could settle the count (see notes file).

title: Detentions at the 11 December 2019 Dispur march: India Blooms (UNI/IBNS) reports that 'a number of student union leaders were arrested by the police during the
establishes: Single source. 'Arrested' is the wire report's word; whether these were formal arrests or detentions is not established. State-wide figures are in HIST-COT-009 and are not specific to this march.

title: Who gave the order for the lathicharge and tear gas against the Cotton University and Guwahati students' march on 11 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document
establishes: Sources read that were checked for this and are silent: Deccan Herald 11 and 12 December 2019, India Blooms 11 December 2019, The Tribune 11 December 2019, The Assam Tribune, The Sentinel 20 December 2019 and 11 January 2020, the PTI report of the AHRC notice, the Assembly replies as reported. Press reports name the state police chief and the Guwahati police commissioner as holders of those offices in relation to the curfew (see HIST-COT-005, HIST-COT-006); that does not show either gave any order for force. No FIR, station diary, deployment order or magisterial inquiry report has been read. Whether the order was written or oral is unknown.

title: A curfew was imposed in Guwahati on the evening of 11 December 2019. The Assam Tribune says 'Curfew has been imposed for an indefinite period in Guwahati from 6
establishes: Curfew existence is corroborated by three sources. The issuing authority is NOT ESTABLISHED: the press attributes announcements to two different offices (the state police chief to PTI; the city police commissioner for a Section 144 order), and the issuing order itself was not read. The News Mill account of Section 144 is single-sourced. Timing matters: Deccan Herald's report of the lathicharge was published at 13:12 IST and India Blooms at 17:43 IST, both before the reported 6:15 pm start, so on the reports read the curfew was not in force when the Dispur march was dispersed. Whether any prohibitory order was already in force for Kamrup Metro at that earlier hour is unknown. The order should be requested (district magistrate Kamrup Metro and the police commissioner, Guwahati).

title: On the evening of 12 December 2019, Deccan Herald reports a unified command meeting in Guwahati 'decided to hand over the charge of law and order to the Army',
