establishes: Single source. The unified command's membership is not given, and no minutes were read. It does not show who ordered force on 11 December. Deccan Herald also reports the state government called in two senior IPS officers and gave one 'the charge of law and order'.

title: Complaints to the Assam Human Rights Commission (AHRC). PTI reports (19 December 2019) that the Cotton University Students' Union and students of other colleges
establishes: The complaints are allegations by the complainants. The filing is corroborated by three reports, but the complaints themselves were not read. The PTI text says the deaths were five and the complaints concern 11 December; the death count is disputed elsewhere (HIST-COT-012). The Assam Tribune page's byline date reads 2010 and is wrong; its dateline is 19 December.

title: AHRC response: PTI reports the AHRC 'has taken suo-motu cognizance' and issued notice to the Assam Chief Secretary to constitute a high level committee to probe
establishes: Single wire source for the notice; the AHRC order was not read. The notice as reported concerns the state-wide protest, mainly the deaths, and does not address the Dispur march specifically. Whether the Chief Secretary's report was filed, and any AHRC outcome, was not found (see HIST-COT-016).

title: FIR and case counts, state-wide, covering the whole state and extending beyond the Cotton University march. PTI reports the Chief Minister told the Assembly in
establishes: The two sets of figures were given at different dates and cover different periods, so they are not a conflict. Neither says how many cases concern the 11 December Dispur march or Cotton University students. Replies were not read; reported by PTI and EastMojo.

title: Any FIR registered over the 11 December 2019 Dispur march, whether against students, organisers or police, and any FIR against police for the lathicharge or tea
establishes: Searches did not surface an FIR number, police station or complaint to a magistrate for this march. The FIR register of the police station with jurisdiction over Dispur and Panbazar, and the Guwahati police commissionerate, would hold this.

title: State-wide force figures for 9 to 20 December 2019, as stated by the Chief Minister in the Assam Assembly (reported by PTI): 25 incidents of firing, 19 cases of
establishes: The December 2021 and March 2020 injury figures differ (20 civilians against about 48), and cover different periods or counting; the difference is not explained in either report. Neither is specific to the Dispur march. Marked REPORTED because the periods stated differ, so the label DISPUTED is withheld.

title: SEPARATE FROM THE MARCH: firing deaths of 11 and 12 December 2019 in Guwahati. The number killed by police fire is DISPUTED. Assam government, via the parliamen
establishes: Victims are not named here: at least one was reported to be a minor and the rest were not confirmed from an official document by this research. These deaths occurred on 12 December (and in one report 11 December) at separate places and are not part of the Cotton University march record. Who ordered the firing is not established in any source read (the Sentinel report of the Lok Sabha member's demand, and the AASU report, both say nothing on who ordered it). The government's reported explanation in March 2020, per a paywalled Millennium Post abstract only (unread beyond the abstract and uncited), was that police fired in the air and missed.

title: Whether any of the firing victims were students: a Gauhati High Court public interest petition, as reported by North East Now on 27 February 2022, describes one
establishes: Single source for the student description, and it is the petitioners' characterisation reported by a news site; the order was not read. This is recorded as a separate item as instructed and not folded into the Cotton University march record. Do not name the victim without a court order or official document that names them. A second source (school or hospital record, court filing) is needed before this can be promoted.

title: Gauhati High Court public interest petition on the deaths of 12 December 2019. North East Now reports that on a Friday in February 2022 a bench of the then Chie
establishes: Single secondary source; order and petition not read; the case number is not given. This concerns the firing deaths and leaves the Dispur march lathicharge out of scope. The state's affidavit, if filed, would be the highest value document on who authorised force (see SOURCING.md section 3). Outcome not found.

title: Magisterial inquiry: EastMojo reports the parliamentary affairs minister told the Assembly on 2 March 2020 that 'a high-level magisterial inquiry into the CAA p
establishes: The inquiry concerns the killings and leaves the Dispur march out of scope. Who ordered the inquiry and who conducts it are not stated in the reports read; its report was not found. The AASU statement conflicts in tone with the minister's statement and the two are not reconciled by any source read, so whether an inquiry was effectively under way by December 2020 is not established.

title: Outcomes: the Chief Secretary's report to the AHRC, any AHRC order, the magisterial inquiry report, any prosecution or disciplinary action against police for th
establishes: To be requested: AHRC case file; Home and Political department; district magistrate Kamrup Metro; eCourts or the Gauhati High Court registry for the petition. See the notes file.

title: Police in Varanasi arrested a group of anti-CAA protesters in the Chetganj area on 19 December 2019, as they were marching towards the Beniabagh ground. Several
establishes: Occurrence is consistent across four outlets that did their own reporting or relayed PTI. No police record, FIR or court order was read. Counts conflict: see HIST-VNS-002 and HIST-VNS-003. The Wire and Sabrang place the arrests in Chetganj; the Quint gives no location; Scroll says Beniya Bagh. No finding is made on whether the protest was peaceful. Police and the protesters' supporters disagree (HIST-VNS-005).

title: The number arrested on 19 December 2019 is DISPUTED. Versions: 59 (The Wire, citing the court bail hearing; PTI via Deccan Herald: 'Fifty-nine people were arres
establishes: The figures are not necessarily inconsistent. A plausible reading is that about 59 to 70 were arrested in Chetganj, more elsewhere (Badagaon), and 56 or 57 appeared in the bail proceedings, but no source states this reconciliation, so this archive does not adopt it. Only the Quint attributes a number to a named office (the SHO of Chetganj station, 68). Another outlet's summary attributed 54 arrested in Beniyabagh to the SSP; that page was not fetched and is not cited. Scroll's 'arrested' versus 'charged' (69 versus 56) is the only source that distinguishes the two.

title: The number of BHU students among those arrested on 19 December 2019 is DISPUTED. Versions: 19 BHU students (The Wire and Madhyamam); 25 of about 70 from BHU, fr
establishes: Range across sources: 12 to about 35. No police or BHU list of the arrested was read. Scroll.in's video page says a BHU student refused his degree at convocation because about 70 students were in jail. Some of these accounts count activists and non-students together, which may explain part of the spread. Not all arrestees were students: the sources describe activists, a research scholar at IIT (BHU), parents of infants, and more than 10 senior citizens aged 60 to 80 (SabrangIndia). A BHU spokesperson is reported elsewhere as saying students' presence could not be confirmed without a police list; that report was seen only in a search summary, so it is not cited.

title: What police did at the time of the arrests is thinly documented. The FIR, as described by Scroll.in, says the protesters 'became aggressive, attacked the police
establishes: Attribution: the FIR account is the police's; 'absolutely no violence, no damage of even a rupee' is an anonymised activist quoted by Scroll; the lathi claim is Amnesty relaying a relative, and it is not tied to 19 December or to Chetganj. Scroll found no injuries among the Varanasi arrestees. National Herald also reports that over a dozen people were injured and a young child died during police lathi charges in Varanasi in the weeks of protest; those events (the Bajardiha protest of 20 December 2019 and others) are separate incidents and are not recorded here, and the child is not named. Police also published a photograph of unidentified protesters and offered a reward for information (The Quint, 20 December 2019).

title: Police and the protesters' supporters give opposing accounts of the 19 December 2019 protest. Police position, as reported: the group violated prohibitory order
establishes: Both versions are allegations by the party that made them. No court has made a finding on what happened on the street in the sources read. The charge on arrest (Section 151, preventive arrest) differs from the FIR sections in HIST-VNS-008; SabrangIndia says other charges were added at the station. Neither SabrangIndia nor Scroll names the police officer who made the statement or the FIR registrant.

title: Who gave the order to arrest the group on 19 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read names the officer or office that ordered the arrests. Reports name o
establishes: Level of office: the only institution named in the sources is the Varanasi police. Whether the decision was taken at station level (Chetganj), by the circle officer, the SSP, or on a direction from the district magistrate or from the state police headquarters is unknown. No individual is named, because no primary document read names one. Documents that could settle it are listed in HIST-VNS-015.

title: Who gave the order for any force used against the group: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read documents the use of force at Chetganj on 19 December 2019 beyond the F
establishes: Related but separate: in a Beniabagh protest on 23 January 2020, police 'chased away' protesters (PTI via Deccan Herald, 23 January 2020) and later sought warrants against 12 persons (Scroll.in); that is a different date and is outside this record.

title: A statewide Section 144 CrPC order was announced for Uttar Pradesh for 19 December 2019. The Director General of Police, O. P. Singh, tweeted on 18 December 201
establishes: What is established: the DGP announced the order and no permission for gatherings was given. What is not: which authority legally issued it and signed it. The sources read do not reproduce the order, its number or its signatory. Scroll's wording ('the state government') and the DGP's tweet are the only attributions. Under the CrPC such orders are ordinarily made by district magistrates or other authorised executive magistrates, but this archive makes no claim about who made this one without the document. The sources are PTI-based and a Kerala newspaper, so independence is limited.

title: Separate local Section 144 orders were also in force in Varanasi in December 2019. SabrangIndia (4 January 2020) reports orders from 11 December 2019 to 5 Febru
establishes: Single source. The ADM is named in the source as a quoted official. No document says he signed or ordered anything, and this archive makes no such claim. Whether these local orders or the statewide one was the basis for the 19 December arrests is not stated by any source. SabrangIndia says police described the arrest charge as violating prohibitory orders.

title: FIR and charges. Scroll.in (25 December 2019) reports that 56 activists were charged under Indian Penal Code sections 147, 148, 149, 188, 332, 353 and 341, plus
establishes: The FIR text itself was not read, so this is not VERIFIED. Neither outlet gives the FIR number, the police station of registration or the date of registration. Quint says charges were against those arrested; Scroll says 56 of 69. The two outlets agree on sections, which suggests a common basis in the FIR or police briefing, so they may not be wholly independent. These are charges as alleged by police; no court finding of guilt is recorded.

title: A separate case concerned pamphlets: SabrangIndia (2 January 2020) reports that three of those granted bail were taken into custody on another charge over distr
establishes: Single source. The three are not named here. The outcome of that second bail application is not in any source read.

title: Bail. A Varanasi Additional Sessions Judge granted bail around 1 to 2 January 2020 to most of those held. The Wire: 57 of the 59 who applied, on two bonds of Rs
establishes: The grant of bail is not in doubt. The count is: 56 (Sabrang, DH headline), 57 of 59 (Wire, Madhyamam), 58 on a literal reading of the DH lead. The Wire and Madhyamam say 57 applied out of 59 arrested, which would leave two who did not apply or were not released; no source says who or why. The Wire gives the judge as 'S. K. Pandey' and Sabrang as 'Sarvesh Kumar Pandey', which may be the same person, and no order was read. Cases had been listed for 1 January 2020 because of the holiday season (Sabrang). The case number and the bail order are not online in any source found.

title: Length of detention. The arrested were held for roughly two weeks: the couple released on bail had been in custody for nearly two weeks (The Wire; PTI). Amnesty
establishes: The Amnesty claim is an NGO allegation about Varanasi arrests between 11 and 23 December 2019 generally, including the 19 December group. The Quint video page says eight students were released five days after the arrests; that is not consistent with the general two-week figure and is not reconciled in any source read.

title: BHU administration. Scroll.in (24 December 2019) reports that the BHU administration 'issued a statement barring students from participating in the protests'. O
establishes: The Joint Action Committee is quoted by The Wire as saying 'both the university and the district administration slap charges against them'; that is an allegation by the committee and no document was read. The text of the BHU statement was not found.

title: Outcome of the case: not established. No source read reports a charge sheet, framing of charges, trial, discharge, acquittal, quashing or withdrawal in the FIR
establishes: Not searched: eCourts for Varanasi district court by party and date, Allahabad High Court, the UP government's notified withdrawal of cases (if any), NHRC and UP SHRC registers. A search of the sources found no Allahabad High Court petition, NHRC order or magistrate inquiry on this event, which is absence of results in a web search and not evidence that none exists.

title: Records that could be requested to establish who gave the order. (1) Chetganj police station: the FIR and its date and time, the general diary (GD) entries of 1
establishes: This is a request list. It asserts no finding. No document on it was obtained or has been seen. Routes: RTI to each public information officer; the UP RTI rules and fee should be checked against current text before filing. Ask the same question at each rung (station, circle, SSP, DM, Home Department) so that any 'not us' reply is itself evidence.

title: Chennai city police entered the Marina campus of the University of Madras on the evening of 17 December 2019, during a student protest against the Citizenship (
establishes: Three outlets, with NDTV and PTI reporting from their own sources. No court or police document read. The News Minute (17 December 2019) puts 'over 100 police officials' around the campus and 'about 10' on it; those figures come from the reporter and are not confirmed elsewhere. The Hindu's Chennai report says protesters numbered over 500, PTI says about 50, and The News Minute says about 80 marched; the protest size is DISPUTED and is not needed for the occurrence.

title: Two students of the University of Madras were taken into police custody on 17 December 2019 and held at a police station for questioning or detention. The Hindu
establishes: Whether this was a detention or an inquiry is the police's characterisation against the students' and the press's. Station is DISPUTED between reports: Triplicane (Scroll, The News Minute 17 December), Mylapore (The News Minute 18 December), Kotturpuram (The Hindu 18 December, for a group of four). Release time: PTI says late that night; The News Minute 18 December says 1:00 a.m. on 18 December after the college administration phoned the station. The two are unnamed here; the names appear only in press reports.

title: Number and place of persons detained around 1:30 p.m. on 17 December 2019 is DISPUTED. The Hindu (18 December 2019) says police 'detained four persons' and that
establishes: Version A: two persons (NDTV, PTI, Scroll, The Hindu Chennai report). Version B: four persons (The Hindu, 18 December). Version C: about 80 detained (The News Minute 17 December, a developing story that was later narrowed to two in the same outlet's 18 December piece). No police or court record read that settles it. A station GD entry or detention register would.

title: Allegation of force on 17 December 2019. A witness named in The News Minute said police 'used their lathis to hit the students when they refused to get into the
establishes: These are allegations by a student and a bystander, and a counter-allegation by an unnamed police officer. No medical record, complaint, injury count or video was read. No injuries are reported in any source read.

title: About 70 students of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Kelambakkam campus (Chennai), were stopped by police near Marina Beach at about 1:30 p.m. on 17 Dece
establishes: Single source: The News Minute, 18 December 2019, partly on the account of a Madras University student. The premise that two TISS students were dragged and held for hours is NOT supported by anything read. In that article the two people dragged and held (2 p.m. to about 1 a.m.) were Madras University students; the TISS students were stopped and sent back. The headline's 'nine hours' also differs from the article's own 2 p.m. to 1 a.m. timeline (about eleven hours). Sabrang's TISS page found by search is about 2018 Mumbai events and is unrelated.

title: Whether the university asked for police entry on 17 December 2019 is DISPUTED. Police version: a senior police official told PTI police came 'following a repres
establishes: The police statements are from unnamed officers. No document from the university (letter, representation, minutes) was found or read, and no university statement on the point was found. Onmanorama reports police saying the gate keys were with varsity officials and that police entered 'for safety of the students'. Scroll says police entered 'even after management urged students to call off the protest' and that it is not stated who in the university made any request.

title: Who gave the order for police to enter the campus, to pick up the two students on 17 December 2019, and for any force used: NOT ESTABLISHED. The only attributio
establishes: Searched for a named officer, a commissioner's statement, a university letter, a court filing and a human rights commission notice and found none. The News Minute reports the Greater Chennai police deployment was for 'safety of the students' (19 December 2019 piece), which describes a purpose. Records that could settle it are listed in madras2019-notes.md.

title: On the night of 18 December 2019 police removed students who were protesting inside the University of Madras campus and took them to Triplicane police station.
establishes: Occurrence corroborated by The Hindu, The News Minute and Madhyamam. The figure of about 17 is REPORTED only (The News Minute; The Quint's body text, whose subtitle says two arrested, contradicts itself). The Hindu and Madhyamam give no count. Who ordered the removal is not stated in any of them.

title: Who gave the order to remove the students on the night of 18 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. None of The Hindu, The News Minute, Madhyamam or The Quint states w
establishes: The Hindu reports that all students were barred from re-entering on 18 December and that police placed barricades; the university had closed the hostel (Madhyamam). Whether the closure and the police removal were coordinated is not stated anywhere read.

title: The university announced a holiday from 18 December to 23 December 2019, extended the already scheduled break to 2 January 2020, and closed the hostel. The Hind
establishes: The motive for the holiday is the protester's allegation. No university order was read. Who in the university decided is not stated.

title: Detention counts differ across sources and no official figure was found. Reported figures for 17 and 18 December 2019: two (NDTV, PTI, Scroll, The Hindu Chennai
establishes: No police statement of a count by a named office was read. Injury counts: none reported in any source read.

title: FIR or case against students: The Hindu (police official) and The News Minute report that no case or FIR was registered after the night removal of 18 December 2
establishes: Madhyamam quotes a Madras University professor saying police left the students without registering any case. All three are press statements of police or witnesses. A search of Triplicane, Mylapore and Kotturpuram station registers, or a Chennai police FIR portal search, was not done.

title: Court, human rights commission or inquiry proceedings concerning the Madras University events of 17 and 18 December 2019: none found. No Madras High Court petit
establishes: This records a failed search and not proof that nothing exists. Searches were general web and news searches only. Madras High Court case status, the Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission and NHRC case search were not queried directly. Compare the Jamia matter (HIST-JMI) where a High Court judgment exists.

title: Kamal Haasan, founder of a political party, was barred from entering the Madras University campus on 18 December 2019 and spoke from the gate. A police official
establishes: Bears on who controlled access. The Hindu says he was barred entry; the police statement about keys is from one unnamed official in a single outlet and conflicts in emphasis with The Hindu's report that police placed barricades at the gate. Not corroborated for the key-holder claim.

title: On Monday 10 February 2020 a march called by the Jamia Coordination Committee set off from gate number 7 of Jamia Millia Islamia towards Parliament, against the
establishes: Four reports agree on the march, the place of the stop and the standoff. The Times of India copy is PTI wire, so the count of independent reporting is three outlets plus the wire. Start and end times vary between reports (about 12 noon, 1:30 p.m. and 2 p.m. are all given for the start or arrival). Sukhdev Vihar Metro station was closed for about an hour in the evening (PTI; Delhi Metro Rail Corporation statement in the Times of India live blog). This is a separate event from the 15 December 2019 campus entry (HIST-JMI-001) and the 30 January 2020 shooting (HIST-JMF-001). No document read is a primary record of the day.

title: Police told the marchers on the day that they had no permission to march to Parliament. Reported statements: the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South East), spe
establishes: What is corroborated is that police said permission had been refused. No application for permission, no refusal letter and no name of the office that decided the refusal was found in any source read. Who decided is recorded as not established at HIST-JMA-005.

title: PTI reported that police stopped the marchers and 'appealed them not to go further as there was no permission and prohibitory orders had been imposed'. PTI's li
establishes: One wire report, carried by two sites, so one source. The Indian Express lists sections 186, 353 and 332 plus damage to property and India Today lists three offence descriptions; neither mentions section 188 or any prohibitory order. No order, notification, date, area covered or issuing office was found. A prohibitory order in force on 10 February 2020 is therefore reported by one source and has no document behind it here.

title: Which office issued any prohibitory order in force around the march route on 10 February 2020, under which provision, covering which area and from which date: N
establishes: Searches of news reports from 8 to 20 February 2020 found no report naming the issuing officer or office. See HIST-JMA-003 for the single report that an order existed. The order, if it exists, is a written instrument and can be requested (HIST-JMA-021).

title: Who decided to refuse permission for the march and to stop it at Holy Family Hospital, and at what level of office: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports show officers of th
establishes: The ranks present are recorded at HIST-JMA-006 and HIST-JMA-007. Speaking at the scene is not the same as authorising, and this archive draws no inference from rank to authority. The refusal may have come from the district, the range, police headquarters or the Union Home Ministry; nothing read distinguishes these. The deployment order is requested at HIST-JMA-021.

title: The Deputy Commissioner of Police (South East) and the Station House Officer of Jamia Nagar were at the barricades and addressed the marchers. The Deputy Commis
establishes: Presence and role of the two officers are in several reports. The deployment figure is recorded separately at HIST-JMA-023. A CRPF spokesperson told the Times of India, in answer to the students' allegation of assault by CRPF personnel, 'No such incident was reported' (HIST-JMA-010). India Today reported tear gas and water cannons deployed near Holy Family Hospital; no report says either was used.

title: In the evening the Joint Commissioner of Police (Southern Range) addressed the protesters near Holy Family Hospital and asked them to call off the protest, sayi
establishes: Single source, a live-blog entry. The officer's name appears in the entry; this record gives the office only because the entry does not say he gave any order.

title: Force used by police at the barricades is DISPUTED. Delhi Police version: the Deputy Commissioner (South East) said 'There was no lathicharge', 'There was a min
establishes: Both versions are attributed to those who gave them. PTI added that eyewitnesses denied any lathicharge (Times of India, 10 February 2020). The police said the entire protest was videographed by them (The Hindu), so footage exists on the police side. No court, commission or inquiry finding on the force used was found. The Indian Express report's wording about 'mild force' sits beside the Deputy Commissioner's denial of a lathicharge in the same article.

title: Specific allegations made by students at the Jamia Coordination Committee press conference of 12 February 2020, reported by PTI: that police kicked students on
establishes: These are allegations by named speakers in the source; this record gives none of their names. One wire report. The students brought medical reports (women) and photographs (men) as evidence, per PTI; none was seen here. Allegations of this kind are not findings. India Today separately quoted doctors at the Jamia health centre on blunt injuries (HIST-JMA-010).

title: Injury counts are DISPUTED and none rests on a document read. Al-Shifa Hospital: its director told the Indian Express that 29 protesters came, four were admitte
establishes: The figures count different things (arrived, admitted, first aid, ICU) at different places and times, and are given by hospital staff, university officials and the students' group. The Al-Shifa director told the Indian Express that no external injury was found in one complaint of pain and an ultrasound was awaited. A CRPF spokesperson said no assault by CRPF was reported (Times of India, 13 February 2020). No medico-legal certificate or hospital record was read; those need consent of the patients (SOURCING.md section 6).

title: Nine protesters were detained on 10 February 2020 and later let go. Delhi Police gave the figure of nine (Deputy Commissioner South East to the Indian Express;
establishes: The police sources conflict on where the detained went: a police spokesperson told the Times of India they were detained and 'later produced before the proctor', while a senior police official told PTI they were taken to Badarpur police station and released. Both are police statements. Students said detained students were taken in a bus; no list of detainees, time of release or legal basis was found in any source. The Badarpur station is named only in the PTI report and in the students' allegations (Times of India, 12 and 13 February 2020).

title: Detained students alleged they were beaten, threatened and made to sit on the bus floor so that onlookers could not see them, and were mocked at Badarpur police
establishes: The three reports carry statements by detained students (Hindustan Times on 10 February 2020, then PTI and the Times of India on the 12 and 13 February press conference). That the allegations were made is reported; whether they are true is not established. Treated as an unproven allegation. No complaint or inquiry specific to treatment in custody was found.

title: Who gave the order to detain the nine protesters, to take them to Badarpur police station, and to use any force at the barricades: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source re
establishes: The detentions are described only as acts of 'police'. Records that would show the arresting or detaining officer are at HIST-JMA-021. The Delhi Police describing detention as temporary and the protesters describing beatings in custody are recorded at HIST-JMA-011 and HIST-JMA-012.

title: Delhi Police said on the evening of 10 February 2020 that a case was being registered against the 'violent crowd'. The Indian Express reports the sections as IP
establishes: The police statement was made by an Additional Public Relations Officer, per the Indian Express. The sections are the police's own description to the press; no FIR was read. The reports differ on the sections: only PTI lists section 188, and India Today's third offence (omission to assist a public servant) appears in no other report. The case is against the crowd; no source says any police officer was named in any case (see HIST-JMA-016).

title: FIR number, police station of registration, date, complainant, named accused and any chargesheet for the case registered after the 10 February 2020 march: NOT E
establishes: The Indian Express reported that a case was being registered; neither it nor India Today or PTI names the station. A search for later bail, chargesheet or court reports on this march found none. Sukhdev Vihar police station is named in reports as the place where protesters gathered in the evening.

title: Any FIR, complaint, court petition, commission inquiry, parliamentary question or departmental action about police conduct on 10 February 2020: NONE FOUND. Sear
establishes: This is the absence of a finding. The searches were made in English through a general search engine and the Firecrawl index, and cannot reach eCourts, NHRC or sansad.in case or question records directly, so they establish nothing about whether such records exist. The Delhi High Court judgment of 5 October 2026 on the December 2019 Jamia events (HIST-JMI-016) was not found to mention the 10 February march in the text previously saved by the archive; that was a keyword search for 'Holy Family', '10.02.2020' and 'Badarpur' and is not a reading of the whole judgment. Filing suggestions are at HIST-JMA-022.

title: Jamia's Chief Proctor, at the scene at about 3:00 p.m., appealed to students to retreat: 'You have registered your protest, now please move back. Don't get into
establishes: Records the university's role on the day. The police reportedly said detained students were produced before the proctor (HIST-JMA-011), which no source confirms from the university side. Not a statement about who gave any order.

title: The students allege the police action was 'preplanned' to stop the march by attacking them. Delhi Police say the students were aggressive and forced their way t
establishes: The preplanning allegation is made by the Jamia Coordination Committee students at the 12 February 2020 press conference (PTI). The police statement of 'a lot of patience' is by a police spokesperson, repeated by the Additional PRO. Neither version is supported by a document read. It bears on the order question only in that a plan, if one existed, would be in a deployment or bandobast order.

title: SUMMARY on the order question for 10 February 2020. ESTABLISHED by reporting: Delhi Police stopped the march at barricades near Holy Family Hospital, told march
establishes: The only institution all accounts attribute the action to is Delhi Police, with an unnamed paramilitary component. Whether the instruction came from station, district, range, headquarters or the Union Home Ministry is not stated in any document read. Oral orders may leave no paper (SOURCING.md, Two limits). See HIST-JMA-004, 005, 013 for the individual questions.

title: Where the permission request for the 10 February 2020 march was made, to whom, and what the refusal said: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports say the police 'rejected' or
establishes: No report quotes the refusal or says whether the Committee applied. If an application was made, it and the refusal are with the police office that received it.

title: Records that could be requested from Delhi Police and the Union Home Ministry (the route for Delhi Police under SOURCING.md): the deployment or bandobast order
establishes: The video is mentioned in the Deputy Commissioner's statement to The Hindu on 13 February 2020. The station names come from the reports (Jamia Nagar for the SHO; Sukhdev Vihar for the evening gathering; Badarpur for the nine). Which station holds the FIR is not known. Exemptions for matters under investigation should be expected, and an RTI reply of 'no such record' would itself be evidence (SOURCING.md section 1). No PIO designation is stated here because none was found.

title: Court and oversight records that could be requested or searched: the Metropolitan Magistrate or court record of the case registered after the march (FIR copy, a
establishes: Nothing in this record says such a filing exists. The sansad.in question archive and the eCourts services were not searched directly in this pass, and a search there is the next step. Medical records at Al-Shifa Hospital and the Jamia health centre need the patients' consent (SOURCING.md section 6); aggregate admission counts for 10 February 2020 can be asked for from hospital records without identities.

title: The Deputy Commissioner of Police (South East) told the Indian Express that over 350 Delhi Police personnel, including 12 Station House Officers and eight compa
establishes: One outlet, quoting the officer. The paramilitary force is not named in the statement. A student described police standing in three layers (PTI, 12 February 2020) and the Times of India live blog reported four layers of barricades. A deployment order would show the units; it is requested at HIST-JMA-021.

title: Police in Bengaluru used lathis (batons) on students who tried to march from Mysore Bank Circle towards the Vidhana Soudha on Tuesday 14 September 2021, in a pr
establishes: Four newspapers with their own reporters agree on the date, the place (Mysore Bank Circle, towards Vidhana Soudha, near KR Circle per TNIE), the lathi use and the custody. The sources differ on the scale and character of the force (see HIST-BLR-003 to 005) and on the time of day (HIST-BLR-014). No primary document (police press note, FIR, order, court record) was found or read. The Scholars at Risk entry for the same day lists ACLED data and the New Indian Express, ETV Bharat and Times of India reports as its basis, so it is not counted as independent and is not cited here.

title: The march was organised by the Campus Front of India (CFI), a student organisation. Deccan Herald, The Hindu, the Times of India and The New Indian Express each
establishes: The archive records the organiser only as the sources name it and makes no characterisation of CFI. The Hindu says 'hundreds'. TNIE reports that CFI office-bearers, including its general secretary, were among those taken into custody; individuals are not named here. Crowd size is a range across outlets, with no count from any official record.

title: What force was used, and how to describe it: DISPUTED. Deccan Herald reports that after students 'slamming down the police barricades' the police 'beat them wit
establishes: Two versions: (a) students and CFI: unprovoked or unnecessary force, blows to the head alleged; (b) police, as reported: barricades pushed, officers attacked, force needed to control the crowd. No video was examined and no inquiry finding was found. The archive makes no finding on proportionality or intent. The unnamed 'senior police officer' in TNIE and 'senior cops' in the Times of India may or may not be the same person.

title: Injuries: DISPUTED. Deccan Herald's standfirst says 'Several protesters suffered injuries, including head wounds and fractures, and had to be hospitalised', but
establishes: Count of injured: police say two (TNIE); CFI says many and several hospitalised (TNIE); no outlet gives an independent number. Medical records need the consent of the people concerned, per SOURCING.md; aggregate admission figures could be sought by RTI from the hospital(s) used. ETV Bharat's article states no number of injured and does not say who ordered the lathi charge.

title: Detentions: DISPUTED on the count. Deccan Herald: 'More than 50 were detained by police but released in the evening.' The New Indian Express: 'All the protester
establishes: 'More than 50' (DH) and 'all' of a crowd of 300 or more (TNIE) can describe the same event only if 50 is a minimum and the true total is higher. The sources agree that detention was described as preventive and that those held were released the same day (DH says in the evening). No source gives the legal provision used, the station or stations where people were held, or a list. A detention memo or the station diary would settle the count.

title: The Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) publicly justified the baton charge. Deccan Herald reports that this officer said the protesters 'had defied the pro
establishes: One outlet. The post is named in the claim; the paper also gives the post-holder's name, which the archive does not repeat because no primary document naming the officer was read. The statement is a justification given after the event. It does not say who ordered the charge, or at what moment, or whether the DCP was on the spot. Section 188 IPC is the penal provision for disobeying a public servant's order; the order itself is a separate document (see HIST-BLR-009 and 010).

title: Who gave the order for the baton charge: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document and no named person is given in any source read. The New Indian Express quotes an unnamed
establishes: Level of office: the only offices on the record are the DCP (Central), who spoke for the police, and the Bengaluru City Police, under whose jurisdiction Halasuru Gate station (named by DH as the jurisdictional station) falls. Whether the decision was taken by the officer commanding the bandobast at the spot, by the DCP, by the Commissioner or on instruction from the state government is not stated in any source read. The post-event statements by the state Home Minister or Chief Minister, if any, were not found. Documents that could settle it: the bandobast (deployment) order for 14 September 2021, the wireless and control-room log, the station diary entry, and the DCP's report to the Commissioner. See notes file for the request list.

title: Who ordered the detentions: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Hindu says police 'bundled them into the vehicles and took them away as part of preventive detention'; The New
establishes: The legal provision relied on for 'preventive custody' is not stated in any source read. Whether the detainees were formally arrested, and where they were held, is not stated. The Commissioner of Police, the DCP (Central) and the station house officer are the offices that would hold the paper; none has been asked.

title: The prohibitory order the DCP cited: its issuer, date, area and number are NOT ESTABLISHED. Deccan Herald says police stopped the students 'citing prohibitory o
establishes: No page read here says who issued the session order. In 2021 the CrPC governed, and the BNSS did not apply. An order of this kind is a written instrument with an issuer, a date and an area, obtainable by RTI from the Commissioner's office; the press reports do not mention one, which leaves the question open.

title: A separate, city-wide Covid-period prohibitory order by the Bengaluru Police Commissioner was in force around the date. The Hindu, in a report first published a
establishes: Both pages are from one outlet, so it stays at REPORTED. The Hindu names the post-holder who issued it; the archive records the office only. Whether this is the order the DCP (Central) meant is NOT ESTABLISHED: Deccan Herald links the DCP's remark to Section 188 IPC and, separately, to the legislative session and to 'Covid rules' in the case police promised to register (HIST-BLR-011). Both a Covid order and a session order may have applied; no source says which one was cited. The page for the 27 September extension carries an 'updated' stamp of 22 November 2021; the report text and its first publication date are 13 and 14 September 2021.

title: First information report: as of late on Tuesday 14 September 2021 none had been registered. Deccan Herald reports that police 'promised to register a case again
establishes: One outlet, one night. This is a statement about 14 September only. Whether a case was registered afterwards, against whom, and under which sections, was searched for and not found (HIST-BLR-012).

title: Whether any FIR or case was registered afterwards against the organisers or participants, or against any police officer, over the 14 September 2021 events: UNKN
establishes: Searches by organisation, station name and date returned nothing after the Deccan Herald report. The Karnataka Police FIR portal and the Halasuru Gate station register are the places to look; both are listed in the notes file.

title: Complaints and court proceedings: CFI said it would complain; whether anything was filed or decided is UNKNOWN. ETV Bharat reports that a CFI office-bearer said
establishes: The statement of intent is REPORTED by one outlet; the claim that something was filed has no page behind it, so the record is UNKNOWN. No writ petition, magisterial inquiry, human rights commission case or departmental inquiry was found. The Karnataka State Human Rights Commission and the Karnataka High Court case-status pages are untested routes.

title: Time of the confrontation: DISPUTED. Deccan Herald (published 15:26 IST on 14 September 2021) says students were baton-charged 'on Tuesday morning'. The Times o
establishes: Two outlets say morning, one says afternoon. Station diary and control-room log timestamps would fix it. This matters for the order question because the bandobast order and the log entries are keyed by time.

title: Statements by the state Home Minister, the Chief Minister, the Police Commissioner or the legislature about who authorised the action: UNKNOWN. No such statemen
establishes: A question in the state legislature, or an RTI to the Home Department, would produce an attributable answer. The session was running at the time (DH, TNIE and The Hindu all say the legislature or Assembly was in session), so a question could have been put in that session; the legislature's question lists were not searched.

title: Police and district administration personnel used lathis on protesting girl students at the Dhanbad collectorate (District Collectorate, Dhanbad) on Friday 6 Au
establishes: Occurrence is reported by several outlets with their own reporters (Times of India, Avenue Mail, Dainik Bhaskar, Zee News); the NDTV copy is ANI. No official document was read. No finding on whether the force was necessary or proportionate. Articles call the protesters girl students and Class 12 examinees; their ages are not given in any source read and no individual student is named in this record.

title: Date of the lathi charge: 6 August 2021 (a Friday). Five outlets give it; no source puts the lathi charge itself on 5 August, which appears only for the precedi
establishes: Archive position: 6 August 2021 is what every source that dates the lathi charge says; the 5 or 6 question has no source that supports 5 August for the lathi charge itself. It is still marked DISPUTED as instructed because the Organiser account is ambiguous and the 5 August dharna is the day before. Resolving it needs the district administration's or police's own dated record, for example the Dhanbad station diary entry or the enquiry report. Also unresolved: duration of the earlier protest ('since 2 August' per Avenue Mail; 'last four days' per Times of India), and time of the lathi charge (about 2.30 p.m. per Avenue Mail only).

title: Who gave the order for the lathi charge, at the level of office: the sources name the Sub-Divisional Officer (Sadar), Dhanbad, an officer of the district admini
establishes: All secondary reports; no order, deployment record, station diary entry or enquiry finding was read. Several attributions are allegations by named political figures (a BJP MLA, the BJP spokesperson who asked for an FIR against the officer, a BJP district office-bearer) and are not findings. The archive does not repeat an individual's name here; the officer is named in the cited articles, and no primary document read names or confirms the person. Panchjanya was read only through an automated page summary. Dainik Jagran also reports that injured girls told the enquiry team the lathi charge was done at the officer's word, and that the team declined to comment officially (see HIST-DHN-010).

title: Whether the officer acted on an instruction from anyone senior (Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, or the minister present), and whether any written
establishes: Empty source list by archive rule: the question has no page that answers it. The minister's reported remark on the officer is at HIST-DHN-015. Documents that could answer: the enquiry report, any deployment or duty record for the collectorate that day, the station diary of the Dhanbad police station, and the officer's own written account if one was filed.

title: Injuries reported on 6 August 2021: the Times of India reports that at least two girl students fainted and nearly half a dozen were injured, and that six injure
establishes: The figure 'about six injured' comes from one outlet. No medical record or hospital figure was read. No injured person is named here.

title: Custody on 6 August 2021: the Times of India reports eight of the protesting girl students were 'arrested' and that the Deputy Commissioner assured MLAs the eig
establishes: Corroborated only that some protesters were taken into custody; the count of eight is from the Times of India alone. The furniture allegation is the police or administration's account as relayed by one outlet. No FIR number, section, or release record was found (see HIST-DHN-016).

title: Accounts of what led to the force are DISPUTED. Administration and police version as reported: students tried to forcibly enter the conference room where the mi
establishes: Both sides are reported secondhand by journalists; neither account has been tested by an enquiry finding that was published. No finding on who is correct.

title: An enquiry into the lathi charge was set up. The Jharkhand Education Minister told ANI on 9 August 2021 that the Dhanbad Deputy Commissioner 'has constituted an
establishes: Three independent outlets agree an enquiry exists; they differ on who was named to run it (ADM law and order in Times of India, Additional Collector and City SP in Jagran), which may be two descriptions of one committee but is not resolved. The Deputy Commissioner's first name is spelled differently in Times of India and Dainik Jagran, so no name is recorded. No enquiry order was read.

title: What the enquiry found: NOT ESTABLISHED. No published report, finding, or statement of outcome was located in any source read. Dainik Jagran (9 August 2021) rep
establishes: Empty source list by archive rule. Searches in English and Hindi returned nothing on the report after 9 August 2021. The Panchjanya allegation is a partisan outlet's claim and was read only through a page summary. Record that could settle it: the enquiry report and the Deputy Commissioner's covering note, obtainable by an RTI application to the Dhanbad district administration.

title: Dainik Jagran reports that injured girls gave statements to the Deputy Commissioner's enquiry team that the lathi charge was done at the officer's word, that th
establishes: Single source, Hindi, 9 August 2021. The statements themselves were not read. This is an allegation made by students, relayed by the newspaper, and is not a finding. No student is named in this record.

title: A Dhanbad lawyer raised the lathi charge before the National Human Rights Commission, calling it, in SheThePeople's report of 7 August 2021, 'barbaric and not a
establishes: Single secondary source, read only through an automated page summary. The lawyer's statement is an allegation. Whether a complaint was registered, a diary number assigned, or a report called from the Dhanbad authorities: UNKNOWN, see HIST-DHN-012.

title: Any NHRC response to the Dhanbad complaint (registration, diary number, direction to the Deputy Commissioner or police, report received, closure): NOT ESTABLISH
establishes: Empty source list by archive rule. The NHRC site was reachable in search results but no page about this complaint was found. Route: ask the complainant for the diary number; an RTI to the NHRC; NHRC case-status lookup once a diary number is known.

title: Dainik Jagran reports (9 August 2021, evening) that the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights took cognisance of the Dhanbad lathi charge on the ba
establishes: Single source. No NCPCR document was read. The response, if any, is unknown. Not confirmed that the commission's jurisdiction applied to every student present, since ages are not given in any source.

title: Transfer of the officer: Dainik Bhaskar reports a Jharkhand government personnel department notification issued on Wednesday 11 August 2021 transferring the Dha
establishes: Single source. The notification itself was not read. The government's stated reason for the transfer, if any, is unknown. The link to the lathi charge is the newspaper's characterisation. A transfer is not a disciplinary finding.

title: Political demands and statements after the lathi charge, attributed to those who made them: the state health minister (quoted by Avenue Mail) said the lathi cha
establishes: Statements by interested parties, recorded as statements only. No FIR against any official was found.

title: On Saturday 7 August 2021, during the Dhanbad bandh called against the girls' lathi charge, Zee News reports police used lathis on ABVP workers who tried to ent
establishes: Separate incident, same week. Counts of injured are not given. Panchjanya is a partisan outlet read through a page summary; its claim concerns one unnamed person and is not repeated as established.

title: FIRs relating to the 6 August 2021 events (against protesters, against officials, or on any complainant's application): NOT ESTABLISHED. No FIR number, police s
establishes: Empty source list by archive rule. Route: RTI to the Dhanbad Superintendent of Police for FIRs registered on or after 6 August 2021 relating to the collectorate protest; Jharkhand Police FIR publication, if any, not checked.

title: Court proceedings (High Court writ, magistrate's court, or any other) arising from the 6 August 2021 Dhanbad lathi charge, and any outcome or disciplinary actio
establishes: Empty source list by archive rule. Searches did not cover eCourts, the Jharkhand High Court or Indian Kanoon case lists directly. Next step: search those by party and date range.

title: Police in Lucknow used lathis on people taking part in a candlelight march on the evening of Saturday 4 December 2021. The march was by candidates protesting al
establishes: Independence: NDTV and Aaj Tak have their own reporting and their own timestamps on the evening of 4 December. Deccan Herald has its own byline. NewsClick carries eyewitness accounts. The Quint and Hindustan Times lean on the Samajwadi Party video and are listed in HIST-LKO-002 and HIST-LKO-005 instead. This finds only that force was reported; it makes no finding on whether the force was lawful or proportionate. The video itself was not viewed. No police or government document was found.

title: Date of the incident. Version A: Saturday 4 December 2021 (NDTV published at 10:48 p.m. IST on 4 December; Aaj Tak published at 9:58 p.m. IST on 4 December and
establishes: 4 December 2021 was a Saturday and 5 December a Sunday (checked by calendar). Reports with timestamps from the night of 4 December, and the party tweet stamped 4 December, favour version A, and NewsClick's 'Sunday' also conflicts with the date of its own embedded tweet. The BSP tweet quoted by Sabrang was not seen in its original form, so its date is unchecked. The archive records both versions and does not resolve the conflict by choosing. A police or court document giving the date has not been found.

title: Who gave the order for the lathi charge: not established. None of the pages read (NDTV, Aaj Tak, Deccan Herald, NewsClick, Hindustan Times, ABP Live, The Quint,
establishes: Level of office is not recorded in any source read. Aaj Tak says only that a 'large number' of police were deployed ('बड़ी संख्या में तैनात पुलिस बल'). No deployment order, magistrate's order, station diary entry or police statement was found. Documents that could answer this are listed in lucknow2021-notes.md. Oral orders leave no paper, so the ceiling may be who was present and what was logged.

title: Whether any prohibitory order or permission refusal covered the march, and whether any police or district administration statement was issued about the lathi ch
establishes: Deccan Herald reports that a senior state BJP leader, unnamed, said 'We have no information about the incident'. That is a party statement and says nothing about orders. NDTV, The Quint and NewsClick report no police statement.

title: Number injured. Version A: 'about a dozen protesters injured' (NewsClick, 6 December 2021, reporter's text; the article attributes the lathi-charge details to e
establishes: The 'hundreds' figure is a politician's statement. No hospital record, medico-legal certificate or police tally was found. Aaj Tak also reports that several candidates jumped over a railing to escape; this is the outlet's account, unsourced.

title: Detentions on 4 December 2021: no source read reports any detention in connection with the lathi charge. Whether anyone was detained, arrested or booked that ev
establishes: NewsClick says 'the injured protesters headed towards the Eco Garden' (Sabrang's wording) and that applicants were gathering at Eco Garden afterwards; neither says anyone was held. A separate HRDA allegation of detention on 2 December is HIST-LKO-007.

title: HRDA alleges that on 2 December 2021, two days before the march, police stopped a jobs protest near the Gandhi Statue in Lucknow and held protesters at Eco Park
establishes: Single source, an advocacy group working from its regional consultant, contact with defenders and media reports. It does not say that this protest was by the same group as the 4 December march. No police record of the 2 December detention was found. The persons named in the letter are not named here.

title: HRDA addressed an 'Urgent Appeal for Action' dated 10 December 2021 to the HRD Focal Point at the National Human Rights Commission, asking the NHRC to direct th
establishes: The two HRDA texts differ on date (letter 10 December, web posting 13 December; the posting is itself dated 10 December). No NHRC acknowledgement, case number, call for a report or outcome was found. The letter's own 'Perpetrators' entry reads 'Police officials of Lucknow'; this is HRDA's allegation and names no individual or office. Filed as legal_proceeding only because it is a complaint to a statutory body; it is not a registered case on the evidence read.

title: How the sources describe the people on the march (exact wording). The Quint: 'protesters', 'the protesters'. NDTV: 'a group of people holding a sustained protes
establishes: They were applicants in a recruitment process, so 'teachers' in the Hindustan Times headline and the HRDA letter is loose wording. 'Peaceful' is used by the Samajwadi Party, Deccan Herald, Hindustan Times, Sabrang and HRDA; see HIST-LKO-010 for a report of a clash. No source read gives ages, and no minors are named. title: The reports record a Deputy Superintendent of Police, Law and Order (Patna; described by The Statesman/ANI as 'DSP Law and Order Kotwali'), speaking to reporter
establishes: What the sources say about the DSP is recorded; no inference is drawn that he gave the order. His name is spelled differently across outlets and is not repeated in this record because no primary document names him; the archive should name an individual only on a document. The Statesman and Organiser carry the same ANI quotation, so they count as one origin; The Hindu and The Indian Express carry the same PTI quotation. The two origins (ANI and PTI) are independent of each other. Organiser is a partisan outlet and is listed only as a duplicate of the ANI text; the claim rests on The Statesman and The Hindu/Indian Express. The ANI and PTI quotes describe different statements; they do not conflict. Rank: DSP is a mid-level state police rank; the Senior Superintendent of Police of Patna (see HIST-PDM-005) was also quoted the same day.

title: Injuries on 1 July 2023 are reported with different counts. LatestLY (IANS) says six job aspirants sustained injuries. The Indian Express says seven teachers we
establishes: Version A: six injured (IANS via LatestLY). Version B: seven injured and hospitalised (Indian Express, Express News Service). Version C: a few, no number (TOI). The counts may refer to different groups, times or definitions; none cites a hospital or medical record. No medical record read. Medico-legal certificates require the consent of the injured person (see SOURCING.md section 6); an aggregate figure could be sought by RTI to the hospitals concerned. No injured person is named here.

title: Detentions on 1 July 2023 are reported with different counts. LatestLY (IANS) says over 36 were detained. The Times of India quotes Patna Senior Superintendent
establishes: Version A: over 36 detained (IANS via LatestLY, no attribution to an official). Version B: around 20 detained (the SSP, as quoted by TOI). Version C: no figure given (DSP, as quoted by The Hindu and The Indian Express). The SSP's figure is the only one attributed to a named office-holder, but it is also second-hand through a newspaper, and the report does not say at what hour it was given. The user-supplied figure of 'over 36' comes only from the IANS copy, which was readable through a scraping service although a direct fetch returned HTTP 403. Bail records or the lock-up register of the two police stations would settle it.

title: Two First Information Reports were registered on 1 July 2023, one at Kotwali police station and one at Gandhi Maidan police station, for obstruction in governme
establishes: Single source, and second-hand: the FIR numbers, sections and accused were not seen. Whether any protester was named, arrested or charge-sheeted is not reported. This is the police account of the allegations; it is not a finding that any offence was committed. The FIR text can be sought from the Bihar Police FIR portal if published, or by RTI to the two stations (see SOURCING.md sections 1 and 3). The DSP's statement that a case 'will be registered' (Statesman/ANI) is consistent with this.

title: The police and the protesters give different accounts of what led to the lathi charge. Police version (TOI report, SSP on FIRs): protesters pelted stones at pol
establishes: Both versions are allegations by the party that made them. The Times of India states the stone-pelting as its own narrative as well as through the SSP; the reporter's source is not given. The Indian Express gives a different sequence: a march from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan from about 11.30 am, a verbal instruction to stop, a first lathi charge, then a second round at Dak Bungalow Chowk. TOI adds a further lathi charge near Gandhi Maidan after police chased protesters towards Patna Junction. The sequence and the place of the first charge therefore differ between the Indian Express and TOI. Video of the day (an ANI clip is linked from LatestLY) was not obtained.

title: The Education Department of Bihar is reported by Organiser to have issued a notice warning of strict action against candidates taking part in the protest, citin
establishes: Single source and a partisan outlet; no independent source found for the notice and the notice itself was not seen. The Deccan Herald (PTI, 13 July 2023) separately reports the education department cancelling leave and asking Patna's district administration to identify teachers who had joined street protests, which concerns a later date and is not corroboration of this notice. A copy of the notice could be requested from the Education Department by RTI. Do not promote without a second source. TRACED 14 October 2026, without success: a search for an independent report of this notice, or of the videography instruction, found nothing. A Careers360 report of November 2023 concerns a different warning to newly appointed teachers who form an association and is not this notice. The record stays UNVERIFIED.

title: Organiser reports that 'several petitions have been filed' against the new recruitment rules requiring future school teacher appointments through a BPSC examina
establishes: Single partisan source, no case number. These would be petitions about the recruitment rules. Searches of news results returned later Patna High Court and Supreme Court matters about teachers (2024 and 2025) that were not read and are not linked to this incident. Eligible route: Patna High Court case status and the Indian Kanoon API (SOURCING.md section 3). No NHRC or Bihar Human Rights Commission case on this incident was found.

title: No source read says that any prohibitory order, dispersal order or order to assemble lawfully was issued, read out or recorded on 1 July 2023. The Indian Expres
establishes: No page establishes the existence or absence of a written order. The sources record only the police's statements about permission. The statutory basis was not checked against current BNSS numbering. Records to request: the permission register of the district administration for 1 July 2023, any order by the District Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Magistrate for the Patna Sadar area, and the control room log.

title: On Monday 23 October 2023 Delhi Police detained students from Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia and Delhi University who were marching towards t
establishes: Four independent origins: the PTI wire (read in the Telegraph, Times of India, India Today, The Federal and Madhyamam copies, which count as ONE source), Sputnik India's own reporter, DU Beat's own reporter, and Peoples Dispatch (which relies on organisers' statements and posts). Sputnik says the cordon stopped the march 'just hundreds of metres away' from the embassy. DU Beat says supporters assembled around 2 p.m. near Khan Market Metro station and that a second group marched about an hour later and was also detained. PTI places the gathering near the Taj Mansingh Hotel (India Today version). The archive makes no finding on whether the detentions were lawful.

title: The number of students detained on 23 October 2023 is given differently by different accounts. PTI, quoting a police officer, says 'Nearly 200 students were det
establishes: The 200 figure has a single origin: an unnamed police officer quoted in the PTI wire, which appeared only in the evening update (India Today, 11:37 p.m. IST; The Federal; Madhyamam). The earlier PTI copies (Telegraph 4:39 p.m. IST; Times of India 16:10 IST) say 'some students'. Scholars at Risk repeats 'over two hundred' and is derived from those copies, so it does not add a second source. The figures of 30 and 200 may measure different things (students present at one spot against everyone detained over the day, including the second group DU Beat describes), so the conflict is recorded without picking a side. No station-wise list or official count was found. The Federal page shows a time stamp that conflicts with its own metadata, so no time is taken from it.

title: Delhi Police's stated position, as reported by PTI: an unnamed police officer said the students were detained 'as they did not have the required permission to h
establishes: Single origin (PTI). The officer is not named in any copy read and no police press note or statement was found. Sputnik India, the only other reporter read who describes the police side, does not quote any officer. Under the archive rule this stays REPORTED until a second independent report or a police document is found.

title: Allegation of force: the protesting students alleged they were 'manhandled' by police. The JNU Students' Union president said many students sustained injuries a
establishes: Allegation and denial are both attributed. The archive makes no finding on whether force was used, its degree, or intent. No video was viewed by the archive, no medical record or complaint was found, and no independent reporter's eyewitness account of force was found. The Peoples Dispatch sentence is written in the outlet's voice but rests on organisers' statements and posts, so it is not treated as an independent observation. Sputnik India, whose reporter was present, mentions no force and no injuries.

title: The number and nature of injuries on 23 October 2023, and whether anyone was treated in hospital: NOT ESTABLISHED. The only statement found is the JNU Students'
establishes: No injury count, hospital name, medical-legal record or complaint to a commission was found. A search snippet from an SFI Facebook page mentioning injured activists and release at 7:15 p.m. could not be fetched (Facebook is blocked to the scraping tool), so it was not read and is not cited; it is also not confirmed to refer to this date.

title: Which police stations the detainees were taken to, and when each person was released: NOT ESTABLISHED. PTI says the students were taken to 'different police sta
establishes: The two accounts agree that detainees were bussed to police stations; the stations are not named in any source read. The 'later released' detail is single-origin (PTI). Station names and release times would be in the station diaries and detention registers listed at HIST-ISR-013.

title: Whether any detained student was formally arrested, booked or charged after 23 October 2023: NOT ESTABLISHED. Sputnik India wrote on the day that it was 'unclea
establishes: No FIR number, charge sheet or police statement on charges was found in the sources read. Absence from the sources read is not evidence that none exists.

title: Who gave the order to detain the students on 23 October 2023: NOT ESTABLISHED. The only attribution in any source read is to 'a police officer' (PTI), unnamed a
establishes: Level of office: the institution all accounts name is Delhi Police, which reports to the Union Home Ministry and has no reporting line to the Government of NCT of Delhi (see sourcemap/CLAUDE.md). Whether the decision was taken at station, district (the embassy area is in New Delhi district, which this research did not confirm from a document), range or headquarters level is unknown, and the same goes for who commanded the barricade line. No individual is named because no primary document names one.

title: Sputnik India reported that, in anticipation of the protest, Delhi Police 'imposed Section 144 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)', which it described as pre
establishes: Single source for the s.144 claim (Sputnik India, 23 October 2023). The order itself was not found: no text, date, area covered, duration or signatory. On 23 October 2023 the CrPC still governed (the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita took effect on 1 July 2024), so CrPC s.144 is the right frame for this date, but that is the archive's reading of the calendar and the order's actual legal basis is unverified. A Delhi Police search result from 2026 about section 163 BNSS orders refers to different events and is not used.

title: Who issued any prohibitory order covering the Israeli embassy area on or before 23 October 2023, and at what level of office: NOT ESTABLISHED. Sputnik India say
establishes: Which Executive Magistrate or police officer held the power to issue such an order in Delhi in October 2023 was not checked against the statute or a notification in this research, so no office is asserted. No individual is named because no primary document names one. If an order exists, it should name its issuer and be dated; asking for it is item HIST-ISR-013.

title: Further action on 24 October 2023: Peoples Dispatch reported that students marched near the Israeli embassy and chanted on 24 October, after hundreds of student
establishes: Single source, and the outlet links to organisations' social posts it relies on. Not checked against any second report. No detentions on 24 October were found.

title: Court proceedings arising from the 23 October 2023 detentions (writ petition, bail application, quashing petition, or contempt): NOT ESTABLISHED. None was found
establishes: Searched for a Delhi High Court or NHRC matter on this incident and found none. Results about a 2026 Delhi High Court petition by a different person concerned different events and are not used. A case listed under a name the archive does not know would not appear in a news search; eCourts and the Delhi High Court case search by party name have not been run.

title: Records that could be requested to establish who gave the order and what was done, none of which has been seen: (1) any prohibitory order under CrPC s.144 cover
establishes: Delhi Police is a Union authority for RTI purposes, so requests go through the Union portal (see sourcemap/CLAUDE.md). Retention schedules may already have destroyed some of these three years on, and a reply saying so is itself a record. An RTI applicant's name can be disclosed under section 11 where third-party information is involved, so any task here carries exposure_risk. Note that at the 2023 date the CrPC provisions apply to the order's legal basis, and the BNSS does not.

title: On 28 March 2023, during the annual fest of Indraprastha College for Women (IPCW), Delhi University, men allegedly scaled the boundary walls and harassed studen
establishes: Background only. This record is about the fest incident. Hindustan Times (30 March) and DailyO (29 March) date the fest incident to Tuesday 28 March. The Quint's 3 April article on the university inquiry, as read through a summary, says the incident occurred on 29 March, which conflicts with those two and with the PTI text (Tuesday, 28 March). The allegations of harassment are the students'; no court has found anything. The DCP North is recorded here as a speaker for police only.

title: On Wednesday 29 March 2023, members of the All India Students' Association (AISA) and, per Hindustan Times, the Students' Federation of India (SFI) protested ou
establishes: Hindustan Times (own reporter) is independent of the ANI and DCP statements that DailyO and The Quint relay. Hindustan Times says AISA and SFI staged an agitation 'until they were bundled in a police van and removed from the spot because police had not given permission for protest'. DailyO quotes ANI: 'Today, at around 11 am, 30 protestors from AISA, had gathered at IP College of Women. They were asked to disperse as their protest was declared unlawful and no permission was granted. When they didn't, they were removed from there without the use of any force.' DailyO does not name who made that ANI statement; The Quint, as read through a summary, attributes it to the DCP (North). DailyO does not mention SFI; the Quint summary attributes the SFI statements to SFI. Whether removal was a detention and whether force was used is in HIST-IPC-003.

title: Whether the 29 March 2023 removal was a detention is DISPUTED. Police version (ANI via DailyO; DCP North via The Quint): protesters were asked to disperse and w
establishes: Police ANI text read directly on DailyO; AISA and SFI statements read through The Quint's summary only, so their wording should be checked against the page. DU Beat (31 March, via summary) says protesters on 29 March were taken to Burari police station. Scholars at Risk's 15 figure sits on Hindustan Times, DailyO and an AISA post and is not an independent count. Only one injury is reported (SFI, one comrade, arm) and it is SFI's own statement; no medical record was found. Police later (3 April) described a comparable event as 'removed peacefully' and 'No one has been detained' (HIST-IPC-010), the same wording pattern.

title: Counts for 29 March 2023 conflict or concern other people. Police: about 30 AISA protesters gathered at around 11 am (ANI via DailyO). Quint summary: 26 release
establishes: Do not add the 7 or 11 to the protester count. HT's text says 'despite detaining 11 suspects' in the opening paragraph; DailyO quotes the DCP as saying seven men were detained; the Quint summary says 11 people questioned. Those are three different figures for the suspects in the fest case, also unreconciled. Stations: Burari police station named for 29 March by DU Beat and by AISA's 3 April statement; no police document read.

title: Who gave the order to remove or detain the AISA and SFI protesters on 29 March 2023: NOT ESTABLISHED. The only statements read are police statements in the pass
establishes: Level of office: the only institutional actor all accounts name is the Delhi Police, North district, with a DCP speaking. Whether the decision was taken by the station, an ACP, the DCP, or on a request from the college is not stated anywhere read. Records that would answer it: the daily diary entry of the police station with jurisdiction, any order or communication declaring the protest unlawful, deployment order for 29 March, and the detention memo or release record at Burari police station. See the notes file for filing targets.

establishes: Read directly or through fetch summaries; wording of quotes should be checked against the pages. ThePrint's version is a PTI feed item; Outlook and DU Beat are separate reports. Scholars at Risk repeats DU Beat, Outlook and others and is not an independent source. The occurrence is corroborated; the force used is DISPUTED between AISA ('beating students') and police ('peacefully detained'). The march was meant to be at the IPCW gate and shifted to the Arts Faculty because of heavy police deployment (Scholars at Risk, DU Beat). Outlook says 'over 200'; ThePrint says 'Over 200' marched and a student said around 200 gathered at the principal's office.

title: Counts and custody for 31 March 2023 are not established. No source read gives an exact number detained. DU Beat says 'numerous individuals' or 'several student
establishes: Single chain of reporting for the station names (Scholars at Risk, which cites DU Beat and others). The DU Beat piece (via summary) says the detainees were to go to an unnamed station. No police figure found. Injuries: AISA and protesters allege many students were injured, some seriously (Mooknayak, via summary); no medical record or count found. The Mooknayak also reports that AISA's Delhi University secretary said she named an ACP in a medico-legal case document; that is an allegation by her and was not confirmed by any record read.

title: Who gave the order to detain or remove the marchers on 31 March 2023: NOT ESTABLISHED. An AISA Delhi University release of 31 March 2023, reproduced by DU Beat
establishes: Level of office alleged by AISA: Assistant Commissioner of Police, Civil Lines subdivision (North district). The individual is named in AISA's release; this record does not name him because no primary document naming him as the person who gave an order has been read. The release itself (primary for what AISA alleged) was not fetched; DU Beat reproduces it. Whether Section 144 signs were posted (Scholars at Risk) and by whom is HIST-IPC-009.

title: A prohibitory order under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure covering the Delhi University North Campus on 31 March 2023: UNVERIFIED. Scholars at Ris
establishes: The 2023 incident predates the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, so the Code of Criminal Procedure governs; reports use 'Section 144' without more. Who issues such orders in Delhi (the Commissioner of Police or a magistrate) is not established from anything read here and is not asserted. The January official is not named and no office is given. The year of the December order is not printed in the fetched text; it is read as December 2022 from context.

title: A second AISA protest outside IPCW on Monday 3 April 2023 ended with protesters being taken to Burari police station. The count and the word for it are DISPUTED
establishes: DH, TNIE and Careers360 carry the same PTI text; National Herald carries IANS, a separate agency. Scholars at Risk repeats the AISA claim and adds that police reportedly said the students were brought to the police station and later released. Police statements within the same day differ on numbers (10-15 versus 27) and on whether the people were taken to a police station. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers and the gates barricaded (PTI). Note that this event is dated 3 April, and the 29 March event is a separate entry; the user's brief said police and unions contradict each other on detained versus removed, which holds on 29 March (HIST-IPC-003) and on 3 April.

title: Who gave the order to remove the protesters on 3 April 2023: NOT ESTABLISHED. The police statements read say protesters 'were asked to disperse but they did not
establishes: No DCP is named as the speaker in either 3 April report. Records that would answer it are listed in the notes file.

establishes: An unnamed student's allegation in PTI; ThePrint and The Wire read through summaries only. The principal is a public office-holder; her statements were not obtained in any source read. A request to the college for any communication with police on 28 to 31 March and 3 April would show it.

establishes: Hindustan Times (own reporting) and The Quint (via summary). The notice concerns the fest and security lapse only. Outcome of the notice not found.

establishes: One agency (PTI), via a summary of the page. These injuries are from the fest. The Outlook and Deccan Herald versions of the same report were not fetched (one returned HTTP 503, the other was not tried), so this is single-source.
